| 2026-05-30 | **🚀 Perceived-auth-lag fix · third sibling shipped via PR [#684](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/684) (signup chain parallelization) · ~500-700ms speedup on signup completion (~50-65% faster).** Closes the perceived-auth-lag arc started earlier today with PRs [#674](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/674) OAuth button instant loading state + [#676](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/676) dashboard-root loading.tsx polish. Owner directive verbatim *"do what needs to be done"* after I flagged signup chain as honest open follow-up from the previous row. **(1) The bottleneck.** Explore-agent audit had flagged [`apps/web/app/signup/actions.ts`](apps/web/app/signup/actions.ts) `signUp()` server action as a sequential await chain post-Supabase-auth-call: `admin.updateUserById({email_confirm:true})` (~100-200ms) → `if (publicSummaryConsent)` poll loop 5×100ms checking `public.users` row exists (DB trigger race) → `admin.update(public_summary_consent_at=NOW())` (~50-100ms) → `sendEmail(welcome)` (~200-500ms · had comment "best-effort, never blocks" but DID block via `await`) → `captureEvent(signup_completed)` (~50-100ms · also had "fire-and-forget; never block" comment but blocked via `await`). Total ~400-1400ms blocked between auth.signUp returning and the redirect firing. Plus ~600ms auth.signUp itself = **~1-2s total signup pre-redirect wait**. **(2) The 3 side-effects are INDEPENDENT** — none reads what another writes. `updateUserById` flips email_confirm. Consent poll+update writes a timestamp. `sendEmail` sends a Resend transactional. They share only `data.user.id` as input; none consumes another's output. Pre-fix they ran serially for no architectural reason. **(3) Refactor.** Collapse the three into `Promise.allSettled` so total wait = `max(updateUserById, consent, sendEmail)` instead of `sum`. Worst case ~600ms · typical ~250ms. `allSettled` (not `Promise.all`): a single failure doesn't cancel the other two · matches existing per-operation error semantics (consent write was already explicitly "non-blocking" per the [2026-05-19 RA 10173 lock](CLAUDE.md) · sendEmail has a fallback "check your email" redirect branch · only `updateUserById` is load-bearing for `autoConfirmed`). Consent IIFE keeps poll → update sequential WITHIN itself (DB-trigger race against `public.users` row creation hasn't gone away · still need to wait for the row before UPDATEing); IIFE itself runs in parallel with the other two. `captureEvent` drops the `await` → fire-and-forget via `void` + `.catch(() => {})` so the documented "never blocks the signup redirect" intent finally matches the code. **(4) Net signup speedup ~500-700ms (~50-65% faster signup completion).** **(5) Safety preserved.** RA 10173 consent recording: opted-in couples still write `public_summary_consent_at` timestamp within the same server action — just in parallel with other side-effects instead of after them. Auto-confirm UX: `autoConfirmed = (updateResult.status === 'fulfilled')` — same load-bearing semantics as pre-fix `autoConfirmed = true` (set only after `updateUserById` awaited without throwing). Per-operation observability: each `allSettled` result's rejection branch logs a `console.warn` so failures show up in Vercel runtime logs. Error semantics strictly improved: pre-fix if `updateUserById` failed, consent + email never ran; post-fix they still run (independent) and can succeed independently. **(6) Architecture.** Next.js server actions on Vercel default to Node runtime. Fire-and-forget promises (the post-redirect `captureEvent`) continue executing in the same Node process after the redirect response is sent. Safe for non-critical side-effects today. If `captureEvent` ever moves to Edge runtime would need `ctx.waitUntil()` — but server actions run Node by default, so `void` + `.catch()` is the right pattern. **(7) PR [#684](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/684)** (merged 2026-05-30T07:14:16Z · +122/-77 single file `apps/web/app/signup/actions.ts` · 2 edits: parallelize the 3 side-effects via `allSettled` + drop `await` on `captureEvent`). **(8) End-to-end auth-lag arc now resolves both login AND signup paths.** Click Login → instant `Signing in…` (pre-existing SubmitButton) OR `Redirecting to Facebook…` (PR #674) → post-redirect Clean Editorial chrome skeleton (PR #676 root + commit [34c4e92](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/commit/34c4e92) event-home) → page paints. Click Create Account → instant `Creating account…` (pre-existing SubmitButton) OR `Redirecting to Facebook…` (PR #674 — OAuth row mounts on /signup too) → 3 side-effects run concurrently instead of serially (PR #684 · ~500-700ms saved) → redirect to /login?ready=email → instant `Signing in…` → dashboard chain per login path. **(9) Verification.** `pnpm -F web typecheck` clean · `pnpm -F web lint` no new warnings · PR auto-merged on green per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]]. **(10) Production smoke verified** earlier in session via curl: `/login` + `/signup` HTML on www.setnayan.com both render OAuth buttons with `aria-busy="false"` (SubmitButton signature) · Google + Facebook brand SVGs intact · `pendingLabel` props serialized into the React client-component boundary · Clean Editorial chrome classes preserved verbatim. PR #684 not yet visible via curl since its effect is server-side runtime behavior (not HTML structure) but CI typecheck+lint+bundle all passed. **(11) Memory rule alignment.** Per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]] `signUp()` server action remains form action for `/signup` · unchanged · no new routes / components / exports. | 2026-05-31 | **🔧 Service-worker cache bump so the new gold logo actually propagates (PR [#698](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/698) merged · Vercel production deploy).** Owner reported the logo still showed the **old orange-red tile** on dashboard / website / login / everywhere after PRs #695 + #696. **Root cause (verified via `curl`):** production was already serving the new gold mark (`/brand/setnayan-mark.svg` → `#cb9e4b`, etag match) — the staleness was the **service worker** `apps/web/public/sw.js` (registered in `layout.tsx:343` on every page), which serves all images **CacheFirst** from a statically-named cache (`setnayan-images-v1`, 30-day max-age). So `<img src="/brand/setnayan-mark.svg">` + the icon SVGs were served off each returning visitor's device cache, bypassing the deploy entirely. **Fix:** introduced a single `VERSION` constant and bumped `v1` → `v2` (renames all 4 caches: shell/images/static/fonts). On next page load the browser detects the changed `sw.js` → installs (`skipWaiting`) → the existing `activate` handler deletes the prior `setnayan-*-v1` caches (now outside `KNOWN_CACHES`) + `clients.claim()` → subsequent image fetches miss → re-fetch the fresh gold mark. **Self-heals on next visit, no user action.** Future same-name asset swaps (logo/favicon/icon) now only need a one-line `VERSION` bump. **Owner-side caches the SW can't reach** (flagged): the browser-tab favicon has its own persistent cache (hard refresh / browser restart), and an already-installed PWA keeps its home-screen icon until re-added. Minor note: with very few picks (short content) the last header may sit in-flow just above the recap rather than in the tight pile — still fully visible; pins cleanly with more content. Per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] auto-merged · per [[feedback_setnayan_button_preservation]] structural move only (no button moved). Follow-up to #717/#718. The repro harness `_pba_verify.html` was authored by the owner; left in place. **`.docx` mirror for CLAUDE.md deferred** (large file; `.md` decision log is canonical). |

| 2026-06-01 | **🎯 VENDOR MATCH PERSONALIZATION — design-locked · per-category preference capture + sort system · amends Onboarding Blueprint §3.0 (venue_setting reconciled back in) · V1.x post-pilot · canonical doc [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md).** Owner brief (pilot day): the wedding onboarding should capture per-category preferences that **sort** vendor search so best-fit vendors surface first; ignored elsewhere — a monogram designer has no headcount); budget = SOFT sort+chip (only total budget captured, no per-category allocation in V1.x). **(3) Per-category preference matrix — the meat (doc §3).** All 10 parents / ~48 tiles mapped to: preference dimension · options · source facet · capture-mode · capacity-bound flag. Capture modes: **🅐 Ask** (lean onboarding · ~4-6 questions) · **🅓 Derive** (aesthetic from mood board 0010 · dietary+religion+ceremony-setting from faith `ceremony_type` 0043 — NOT re-asked) · **🅒 Custom** (Personalized Customization surface + inline "refine" chips while browsing) · **🅑 Basics-only** (hard filters alone). Roughly a third of tiles carry a real style/type preference; rest are filter+ladder governed. The §4 facet dimensions from the taxonomy shrink (religion · dietary · rental · tradition · shoot-type · cart/booth-type · service-type · accessories) **ARE** the preference dimensions; this adds new ones — **venue-type · cuisine · catering-service-style · photo-video-style · coverage · music-vibe**. **(4) Lean onboarding asks (§4):** Reception venue type (owner's flagship) · Cuisine · Photo&Video style · Music vibe · Coordinator service-level (lean-optional) · the vendor-pool question — each skippable + shown only for picked categories. Aesthetic derives from mood board; dietary/religion from faith; long tail to the Customization surface. **(5) Vendor pool — all types vs verified only (§5):** new `events.vendor_pool_preference ENUM('all','verified_only')` · honest both-ways copy (all = supply + startup exposure; verified = curated trust) · verified-only moves unverified to Expand (reason "Unverified"), not a hard ban. **(6) Personalized Customization surface (§6 · NEW, Home):** "Personalize my matches" button on dashboard event-home → single editable store: Basics · Vendor pool · Per-category preferences (by 10 folders, each Edit/Delete) · What-you-love picker. Per-row **Delete** clears one preference → that category reverts to pure ladder ("delete any information they no longer want"). **Master "Deactivate all personalization"** toggle → pure ladder everywhere, hard filters still apply, saved prefs preserved (deactivate ≠ delete) — the owner's "deactivate by demand." Event-shared across multi-host (0048) — preferences describe the wedding, not personal taste (contrast: vendor favorites are per-user). **(7) Data model (§8):** `events.vendor_pool_preference` + `events.personalization_active` + new `event_vendor_preferences(event_id, tile_key, dimension_key, values TEXT[], source, updated_at)` · match = array-overlap (`&&`) between captured values + vendor facet tags · derived prefs written `source='derived'` so they're overridable. Vendor-side facet tags = the deferred 0044 `canonical_service_schemas` attributes (this work depends on that DB substrate landing — "Matches your preference" needs vendors carrying facet tags). **(8) Threads into shipped surfaces (§9):** the canonical `fetchWizardVendorRecommendations` query gains the preference partition + hard-filter params + return-excluded flag (single place the sort lives → Category Search overlay PR #711 + `/vendors` marketplace + Plan+Budget accordion "Find more" + Setnayan AI vendor-pick cards all inherit it); `?match=`/`?venue=` URL filters (PR #305/#311) compose as the hard/derived end of the same system. **(9) venue_setting reconciliation (§10):** owner's reception list (events place · hotel function hall · convention center · garden · destination) is richer than the shipped enum (`banquet_hall·garden·beach·destination·heritage·outdoor_tent·civil_registrar`) → proposed extended set (hotel_ballroom · events_place · convention_center · garden · beach · resort_destination · heritage_hacienda · restaurant_private · tent_open_field · clubhouse; civil_registrar stays a ceremony axis) · extends the enum that already drives `?venue=` (PR #311) · needs migration + vendor re-tag. **Reconciles the Blueprint §3.0 "venue_setting moved OUT of onboarding" lock:** region stays the *area* hard-filter basic; venue *type* returns as the VENUE-category *preference* (soft sort), not a top-level basic — both coexist. This is an explicit owner-directed amendment. **(10) 7 flagged forks for owner (§11):** (1) vendor-pool default = **all types** (recommended · supply + startup exposure · verified-only is the safer-trust alt) · (2) budget = **soft** (no per-category allocation yet) · (3) preference = **labeled groups** not blended boost · (4) onboarding question count = **lean 4-6** shown only for picked categories · (5) pax hard-filter = **capacity-bound tiles only** · (6) adopt the **§10 reconciled venue_setting** list · (7) **"on the vendor app"** read conservatively as the couple-side vendor search (marketplace+overlay+accordion) — a separate "vendors see aggregate demand in their area" feature is a promising-but-distinct future item, flag if owner meant that. **Affected files this row:** NEW [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) at corpus root (12-section self-contained design lock · full per-category matrix) + its `.docx` mirror · CLAUDE.md (this row). | 2026-06-01 | **📳 Vendors tab — cross-platform haptics wired (PR [#724](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/724) merged · `ceca76e` · Vercel production deploy).** Owner (pilot day): *"haptics are not yet included."* The haptic feedback was in the locked spec ([`Vendors_Plan_Budget_Tab_Spec_2026-05-31.md`](03_Strategy/Vendors_Plan_Budget_Tab_Spec_2026-05-31.md) §2D "gentle snap+haptic" · §12 "both-axis snap+haptic") but never implemented — only an Android-only `navigator.vibrate(7)` existed on the coverflow rail-snap. **New shared util `apps/web/lib/haptics.ts`** — `haptic(kind: 'tick'|'select'|'confirm', opts?)` with two engine-specific paths, both degradation-safe: **(a) Android Chrome / installed PWA** → `navigator.vibrate` (real motor pulse · `tick`=8ms · `select`=14ms · `confirm`=[16,36,22] pattern); **(b) iOS Safari 17.4+** → toggles a hidden `<input type="checkbox" switch>` which fires a system haptic. **Apple blocks `navigator.vibrate` entirely**, so the switch-toggle is the ONLY web haptic path on iPhone — and it MUST run synchronously inside a tap gesture (outside a gesture, e.g. a scroll rAF callback, it silently no-ops); **(c) older iOS / desktop / SSR** → silent no-op (`typeof window` + try/catch guards · `getSwitch()` lazily creates one off-screen `aria-hidden` `tabindex=-1` label/input, reused). **Wired moments (Vendors tab only · scoped tight for pilot day):** **Lock this pick** → `confirm` (the key "I chose a vendor" moment · `onClick` on the form-submit button, fires in-gesture before the server action) · **Add** in the category-search overlay → `select`, fired **synchronously at the top of `add()` BEFORE the `saveVendorToPicks` await** (post-await loses the iOS gesture context · so optimistic-on-tap is both the right UX and the only iOS-compatible timing) · **arm-remove** (× tap-to-confirm) → `tick` · **confirm-remove** (Remove submit) → `select` · **coverflow rail-snap** → the existing Android `navigator.vibrate(7)` consolidated onto `haptic('tick', { iosSwitch:false })` — `iosSwitch:false` skips the switch-toggle in scroll context (it can't fire outside a gesture anyway + avoids redundant `.click()` spam during fast swipes), so it stays **Android-only**. **Honest limits surfaced to owner:** passive scroll-snap haptics are **Android-only on web** (iOS has no non-tap web haptic path) · iOS interaction haptics need **Safari 17.4+** (older iOS silently no-ops) · guaranteed iOS haptics across every interaction arrive with the **native app (iteration 0052)** where `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` is available. **Verification:** `pnpm -F web typecheck` clean · `pnpm -F web lint` exit 0 · `pnpm -F web build` clean (`/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors` 15.7 kB, +0.4 kB for the util+wiring). **Additive + degradation-safe** — cannot break layout or interactions (no-op where unsupported · all calls guarded). **Entry points** (per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]): no new routes/components/schema/migration — `haptic()` is called inside existing tap handlers on the existing Vendors surface. **Build hygiene note:** `git add -A` initially staged the worktree's `node_modules` + `apps/web/node_modules` symlinks (the repo's `node_modules/` gitignore pattern matches a directory, not a symlink-file) — caught + removed via `git rm --cached` + `--amend` + force-push BEFORE the PR opened, so CI never saw them. Lesson for future worktree PRs: `git status --short` after `git add -A` and strip any `node_modules` symlink before committing. | 2026-06-01 | **🔒 Verified-only marketplace — vendor tier REMODELLED + couple onboarding step 12 removed (owner 2026-06-01).** Owner directive: *"Once they register, they need to get verified first before their services show up on our marketplace. For the moment they are not yet verified, they can only use our dashboard but not use our marketplace. Please modify our vendors tier."* + *"remove step 12."* **(1) The rule.** Verification is now a **hard gate for ANY marketplace presence.** On signup a vendor is **Registered (unverified)** — full dashboard (build profile · packages [draft] · portfolio · calendar · settings) but **zero marketplace presence** (not in browse, not in search, no public `/v/[slug]`, can't receive couple inquiries/bids). They go live only after passing the 12-doc verification. **(2) Tier remodel — a lifecycle *state* + 3 marketplace tiers.** Verification becomes a lifecycle gate, not a tier: **Registered (unverified · dashboard-only · ₱0)** → **Verified (free marketplace floor · ₱0 + verification)** → **Pro (₱2,499/28d)** → **Enterprise (₱5,499/28d)**. **The old "Free" tier is RETIRED** — its two roles split: the *dashboard-only, nothing-public* identity becomes the **Registered state**; the *free-floor-on-the-marketplace* role becomes **Verified**. There is no longer an anonymized-Free vendor in browse. Pro/Enterprise are **offered post-verification** (the vendor onboarding's second phase) — you can't buy marketplace boosters before you're on the marketplace. Full remodelled matrix in [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) §5.1. **(3) Step 12 removed from couple onboarding.** The "Who should we show you? (all vendors vs verified only)" screen is gone — the marketplace is verified-only by rule, so there's no all-vs-verified choice. Couple flow 16 → **15 screens**; `events.vendor_pool_preference` retired. **(4) What this SUPERSEDES:** (a) the **2026-05-15 vendor public-visibility "coming_soon default · unverified vendors show as muted Coming-soon cards"** decision — `vendors.public_visibility` default flips `coming_soon` → **`unverified`** (dashboard-only, not surfaced); the `coming_soon` "muted card on marketplace" state is **retired** (`unverified` · `verified` · `hidden` · `archived` remain); (b) the **2026-05-15 DIY "Verified only" browse toggle** — moot when everything is verified; (c) the **4-tier matrix's Free column** (2026-05-30 amendment #2 §5 / the v2.1 brief §3) — Free is no longer a marketplace tier; (d) **hybrid-anonymity** ([[project_setnayan_vendor_hybrid_anonymity]] + 2026-05-30 amendment #2) simplifies from "Free + Verified hidden-until-first-reply" → **"Verified hidden-until-first-reply, Pro+ shown, venue exception holds"** (Free is gone from the marketplace); (e) `events.vendor_pool_preference` column. **(5) `verified_vendor_count` unchanged in spirit** (Section-3 stats gate · boost-service launch gate still count `public_visibility='verified'`) — but the prior "coming_soon vendors are visible yet uncounted" caveat is gone (nothing visible is uncounted). **(6) Cold-start tradeoff accepted.** The 2026-05-15 `coming_soon` reasoning was "let couples see coverage forming before the verified pool reaches critical mass." The owner overrides it for a clean verified-only marketplace, accepting a thinner early marketplace — recruit-and-verify before launch traffic matters more than visible-but-unbookable cards. **(7) Verification fee UNCHANGED here (flagged open item):** whether Verified is truly ₱0 or carries the one-time ₱1,499 badge fee stays the open pricing question (2026-05-30 amendment #2 + the onboarding drift flag) — this remodel does **not** decide it. **(8) Vendor onboarding already aligns:** signup (onboarding #1) → submit verification → Registered state → verification approved → onboarding #2 (post-verification) goes live + pitches Pro/Enterprise. The only change is that *between* signup and approval the vendor has no marketplace presence (previously a coming_soon card). **Affected files (this row):** [Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html](06_Prototypes/Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html) (couple prototype — vendor-pool screen removed · 15 screens · nav arrays + comments renumbered · browser-verified prefs→account, no crash) · [Onboarding_Blueprint_2026-05-30.md](03_Strategy/Onboarding_Blueprint_2026-05-30.md) (§3.1a step-12 removed + renumbered 13→12…16→15 · "15 screens / 1 net-new" framing · verified-only note · Expand-search "unverified" reason dropped) · [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) (§1 verified-only pool + dropped the verified hard-filter toggle · §4 removed the vendor-pool ask · **§5 rewritten → "marketplace is verified-only" + §5.1 remodelled tier matrix** · §6 removed the pool toggle from the Customization surface · §7 dropped the "unverified" Expand bucket · §8 retired `events.vendor_pool_preference` + noted `public_visibility` default flip · §11 fork #1 RESOLVED · §12 supersedes-list + sequencing step (0)) · CLAUDE.md (this row). | 2026-06-01 | **🎨 Onboarding refinements — Mixed = interfaith multi-select faith (step 3→4) + wedding-date picker gains a 3rd mode "a few dates" (owner 2026-06-01) · prototype-verified · design-lock · V1.x post-pilot.** Two changes on the wedding Add-Event flow ([Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html](06_Prototypes/Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html)). **(1) "Mixed" = interfaith → step 4 multi-select** ("mixed religion on step 3 means step 4 will have multiple choices"). Corrects the meaning of step-3 "Mixed": it is **mixed *religion* (an interfaith wedding · e.g. Catholic & Muslim)**, NOT religious-plus-civil. Step 4 (faith) is now **adaptive**: *Religious* → single-select one tradition · **Mixed → multi-select** the traditions they'll both honor (writes `ceremony_type` + `secondary_ceremony_type`; 2+ allowed; each picked tradition pre-sets its own dietary + religion-match + protocols) · *Civil* → skipped (a "no tradition to set" note in the prototype; the real build skips the screen). Prototype: new `buildFaith()` render-hook reads the step-3 `data-kind` selection + toggles the faith chip group between single/multi + swaps the copy; browser-verified all three states (Mixed → "Which traditions?" with Catholic + Muslim both selectable · Religious → single Catholic · Civil → skip note). **(2) Date picker → THREE modes** (owner asked "single date · multiple single dates · flexible window — what do you think?" → confirmed **all three** via AskUserQuestion). The picker now offers **Exact date · A few dates (2–5 specific candidates) · Flexible window (≤30 days inclusive)**. The case for the new middle mode: *a few dates ≠ a window* — couples carry a shortlist of **meaningful, intentional** candidate dates (engagement anniversary · a numerology/auspicious date · a long weekend · the weekend relatives can fly in) that a contiguous range would bury under in-between days they'd never pick (very PH-natural — the "pwedeng petsa" shortlist, often sukob/numerology-driven). **One backend resolver, three input styles:** exact = a 1-date set · a few dates = N discrete dates · window = a contiguous span — all feed the **same vendor-availability convergence** (a vendor surfaces if free on ≥1 candidate; as vendors lock, intersect their free candidate days → the feasible-date set → the wedding date settles on a candidate they all share, prefer Saturdays then the couple's lean; empty intersection nudges add-a-date / widen-window / swap-vendor). Caps: a few dates ≤5 · window ≤30 days inclusive (already locked). Prototype: 3-button segmented toggle (Exact date / A few dates / Window) + `multi` candidate-set state (seed 1 on entry · tap to add/remove · 5-cap with "Up to 5 dates — remove one to add another" warning · each candidate rendered as a mulberry-filled day) + the why-panel reframes per mode ("Why a few options works" · "Why a flexible window works") · mode round-trips collapse cleanly (multi→exact = earliest candidate · window→multi restores the set) · browser-verified (seed 1 · cap at 5 · toggle-off · 15-screen walk no crash). **Schema:** `events.date_mode` (`exact`/`multi`/`window`) + `events.event_date` (exact / the resolved final) + `events.date_candidates DATE[]` (a few dates) + `events.date_window_start`/`date_window_end` (window); `event_date` stays NULL for multi/window until vendor-availability resolution stamps it. **Affected files (this row):** [Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html](06_Prototypes/Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html) (step-3 `data-kind` + interfaith copy · step-4 ids + adaptive `buildFaith()` + civil-skip note · step-6 3-button calendar + `multi` candidate-set state + `multiReasons()` + `setMode`/`clickDay`/`build`/`updatePick`/`setRange` extended) · [Onboarding_Blueprint_2026-05-30.md](03_Strategy/Onboarding_Blueprint_2026-05-30.md) (§3.0 data map: Kind=interfaith + wedding-date 3 modes · §3.1a screen 3 interfaith + screen 4 adaptive single/multi/skip + screen 6 three-mode + fixed the stale "screen 14"→"screen 13" demo ref after the step-12 removal) · [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) (§1 ascii "available on date · or window-resolvable" → candidate-set · §2 wedding-date filter row → 3 modes + the "Flexible-window date resolution" note generalized to **"Candidate-set date resolution — a few dates OR a window"** covering all three modes via one resolver + screen-13 ref) · CLAUDE.md (this row). | 2026-06-01 | **🎨 Onboarding batch — 5 Golden Rules locked + date modes merged 3→2 (1–4 specific + flexible window) + live 90-day cluster + nugget bank + region "Somewhere else" expand + budget rough-compass→feasibility-nugget + Mixed faith cap-2 + HALAL pre-lock · prototype-verified · design-lock · V1.x post-pilot.** Owner batch on the wedding Add-Event flow ([Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html](06_Prototypes/Onboarding_Wedding_Flow_2026-06-01.html)). **(1) 5 Golden Rules LOCKED for every onboarding screen** ("add this to your skills · same idea as always") → saved as memory [[feedback_setnayan_onboarding_golden_rules]]: (a) **NO SCROLLING** — fit one phone viewport (≈665px body on the 375×812 frame); only "select-from-many" screens (picker · prefs) + results-browse (find-vendor) may page; (b) **Setnayan always visible** — brand lockup (gold `S` mark + SETNAYAN wordmark + step counter) in the top bar on every screen so a screenshot carries the brand; (c) **keep words at their best** so everything fits; (d) **attractive but premium** (Clean Editorial · calm motion); (e) **photos + app icons allowed** where they earn their height. Corollary: **no redundant "Not sure yet" defer-ghosts** — the bottom CTA bar already has **Skip**, so the inline "Not sure yet — we'll set it later" was removed from the date screen (Skip is the defer path · also reclaims height for Rule 1). **(2) Date picker merged 3 modes → 2** (per owner "combine single + specific · up to 4"): **Specific dates** (1–4 candidate dates · 1 date = a valid set, absorbing the old "exact" single mode) + **Flexible window** (≤30 days inclusive · MAXSPAN=29). One backend resolver: candidate-date set → vendor-availability convergence → stamps the final `event_date`. **(3) Live-shrinking 90-day cluster** (owner "starts with 1 date ±3 months · shrinking · up to 4 · then the calendar locks"): after ≥1 specific date picked, the selectable window = `[max(picked)−90d, min(picked)+90d]` (CLUSTER=90) — it naturally shrinks as the set spreads; at MAXMULTI=4 the calendar locks (non-picked days disabled; picked days still removable to swap). **(4) Nugget bank** (`commonReasons`, owner "what is common for the 4 dates · all Saturdays / same month / same season / other ways schedules inter-relate · framed around vendors filling up"): 1 date → "✦ Why this date works" (single-date 5-layer taste); 2–4 dates → "✦ What your dates share" detecting all-same-weekday ("All Saturdays — the prime wedding day…"), all-weekends, all-same-month ("All in December — one month to staff…"), all-same-season, all-numerology (8/18/28), and cluster span — every nugget framed around vendor scheduling ("a vendor only needs one open slot · as schedules fill, we lock the one they all share"). **(5) Step 7 region "Somewhere else" expand** (owner "when somewhere else is picked we show other regions · the first 5 disappear · somewhere else card goes up revealing the rest"): default = 5 top PH regions (NCR · CALABARZON · Central Visayas · Western Visayas · Central Luzon) + a "Somewhere else" card; tapping it collapses the 5, raises "Somewhere else" to the top (gold-wash expanded state + "‹ Show top regions" back), and reveals the remaining 13 regions (Ilocos · Cagayan Valley · Bicol · MIMAROPA · Eastern Visayas · Zamboanga · Northern Mindanao · Davao · SOCCSKSARGEN · Caraga · BARMM · Cordillera/CAR · Outside PH) as a compact 2-col grid — both states fit one screen (571 / 576 px). **(6) Step 9 budget rough-compass → feasibility nugget** (owner "a rough compass shows before they choose · once they choose it disappears and a budget nugget shows · identify if feasible · add No Limit · say this is enough to add services / go premium / allowance above range"): pre-choice = "A rough compass" = per-pax range (pax × ₱3,500–₱10,000, e.g. ~₱700K–₱2M for 200); | 2026-06-01 | **💰 Region-tiered vendor monetization — full model locked (structure firm · peso numbers owner-set/pending) · consolidates + completes the same-day "💰 V1 vendor monetization repriced" row.** Owner confirmed the complete region-pricing model across a multi-turn conversation; market coverage shifts from km-radius to **region** as the basis, and region now drives BOTH the coverage boundary AND the pricing tier — justified on demand (income / booking value) AND supply (regional minimum wage / cost base). **(1) Four region bands** (validated against 2024 GRDP + 2023 PSA family income + 2025 RTWPB regional minimum wage + PH wedding-market data): **Band 1 (highest)** Metro Manila/NCR · **Band 2** CALABARZON · Central Visayas · **Band 3** Western Visayas · Central Luzon · **Band 4 (base)** everywhere else. Data anchors: NCR 31.1% of GDP / ₱513.5k avg family income / ₱658–695 daily min wage; provinces ~₱435–550 wage; BARMM ₱207k income (<½ NCR); provincial weddings 20–40% cheaper than Manila; Tagaytay (CALABARZON) · Cebu (C. Visayas) · Boracay (W. Visayas) the premium destination hubs. **Flags:** Central Luzon is the one debatable placement (income #3 nationally → could be Band 2; kept at Band 3 for lack of a marquee destination magnet — revisit on data) · Davao a candidate to promote from base on volume (wealthy Davao City lumped with poorer Davao-region provinces) · region is a COARSE proxy (within-region spread: Tagaytay vs rural Quezon; Boracay vs Antique) — refine to province/city later if data warrants, acceptable V1 tradeoff. **(2) TOKEN mechanic — universal token + region-weighted burn (the core).** ONE universal "token / Booking Match" + ONE wallet (no per-region fragmentation). Answering a match debits a **region-weighted number of tokens keyed to the EVENT's region**; **burn varies by region, NOT booking size** — so the flat-token lock + value-based-rejection from the prior row are preserved (every NCR match burns the same regardless of a ₱30k-vs-₱1M wedding). Illustrative burn ladder (numbers owner-set): **Band 4 = 3 · Band 3 = 4 · Band 2 = 5 · Band 1/NCR = 6 tokens** = a clean **~2× spread** (tracks per-lead value: income + booking value + competition). Per-token PRICE is **uniform** + cheaper in bigger packs (4/10/25/50/100 — the actual charm-priced SKUs) + the 100-token founder grant retained (now stretches further in cheaper regions — seeds provincial supply). Effective match cost = `burn × per-token price`; illustrative @ ₱100/token → ₱300/₱400/₱500/₱600. **Why universal+burn beats the alternatives:** per-region tokens fragment the wallet (leftover-region-balance); pure per-transaction discards prepaid packs + founder grant + buries V1's manual apply-then-pay in micro-reconciliations; a flat 1-token-anywhere kills the tiering. Decisive: **price the SPEND (burn at match-time, keyed to event region, un-dodgeable), not the PURCHASE (per-region pack prices are gameable — buy cheap-region packs, spend on NCR).** Standard Bark/Thumbtack "credits with variable action-cost" pattern; vendor sees "This match: 6 tokens · you have 40" pre-confirm. **(3) SUBSCRIPTION mechanic — region-DIRECT peso price.** Pro/Enterprise 28-day are a flat recurring fee (not a fungible unit), so they're region-priced **directly** — no burn. Spread **~1.5×** (tracks the operating-cost base / minimum wage, which varies less than per-lead value — so the recurring fee swings gentler than the token). **Base band = today's price** (Pro ₱2,499 / Enterprise ₱5,499) so provinces hold steady (good for the supply you're recruiting) and the **raise lands on NCR + the top bands** where willingness-to-pay is highest (= "raise the tiers" done land-grab-friendly). Illustrative (owner-set): Pro ₱2,499/₱2,999/₱3,499/₱3,999 · Enterprise ₱5,499/₱6,499/₱7,499/₱8,499 (Band 4→1). Annual = the band's 28-day × ~11 (~23% discount) per band. **Priced at the HIGHEST band the vendor opts to cover — NOT a per-region sum** (opt into NCR → pay the NCR sub once, regardless of home base or how many other regions you also cover — closes the arbitrage). **Two reasons it's highest-band-only, never summed:** (a) **the token burn already captures per-region value at every match** — a multi-region vendor pays the 6-token NCR burn on NCR matches + the 5-token CALABARZON burn on CALABARZON matches, so regional value is recaptured transactionally; summing region subs on top would double-tax the same multi-region value; (b) **a per-region sum would punish the dense border coverage we just enabled** (Cavite/Laguna/Rizal serving Metro Manila — billing NCR-sub + CALABARZON-sub ≈ ₱7.5k/28d in the illustrative ladder would push them off-platform). **The multi-region paywall is the TIER, not a per-region fee:** region COUNT is gated by tier (Verified = home region only · Pro = home + 1 adjacent · Enterprise = home + wider/multiple), so breadth is unlocked by climbing the ladder + paying the top band you reach — a vendor can't blanket the country on one cheap sub. **V1.5 escape hatch:** if pilot data shows broad-coverage vendors get too much reach for one flat top-band fee, add a *modest* per-additional-region add-on then (highest band base + small fee per extra region) — NOT built at launch; the token already does the per-region heavy lifting. **(4) km / coverage — RETAINED, scoped within region.** km/distance stays for **transportation cost** (a real per-job expense · already the Transportation line in iteration 0007's per-vendor budget) + nearest-first relevance. The radius now reads as **within-region travel reach** ("20km within Metro Manila"), NOT cross-region reach — existing tier radii re-interpret as Verified 20km / Pro 50km / Enterprise 100km *inside* covered region(s). **Cross-region allowed** via a vendor **declaring the adjacent region(s) they genuinely serve** (handles the dense NCR↔CALABARZON border — Cavite/Laguna/Rizal serve Metro Manila constantly) — km no longer silently bleeds across region lines. **(5) Keying summary:** token → EVENT region · subscription → HIGHEST region the vendor covers. **(6) Consistency with locks:** 0% commission KEPT; flat-per-match-within-region preserved (burn by region not booking size); stacks with the same-day "token raised flat" decision (per-token price rises uniformly for the lead-quality lift × region burn weight = two clean levers); prepaid packs + volume discount + 100-token founder grant + manual apply-then-pay all intact; charm pricing on the SKU prices retained. **(7) NUMBERS PENDING — illustrative only.** The peso figures above (₱100/token; the sub ladders) are a WORKED EXAMPLE to show the shape; **owner sets the finals** — (a) the uniform per-token price + pack discounts, (b) the 4 burn weights, (c) the 4-band sub prices — tuned on pilot data (tokens spent per booking won by category · vendor WTP · couple-side demand density). What's LOCKED is the **structure**: 4 bands + band→region map + universal-token-with-event-region-weighted-burn + region-direct subscription + token ~2× / sub ~1.5× spreads + the keying + km-within-region + declared-adjacency. Gut-check: even at ₱600/NCR-match, a ~1-in-3 qualified-lead conversion → ~₱1,800 cost-per-booking (below the old ₱250×~10 = ₱2,500) and a rounding error vs a 15% commission (₱15k on a ₱100k NCR booking) — the math still favors staying on Setnayan, no gouging. **(8) Implementation cascade (when numbers land — a coordinated pass):** `platform_retail_catalog_v2` per-token price + pack rows + the per-region burn-weight config · `vendor_billing_catalog` region-tiered Pro/Enterprise 28-day + annual rows · token-spend logic debits the event-region burn from the universal wallet · `events.region` (already captured at onboarding step 7) + vendor `declared_regions[]` + `primary_region` · onboarding vendor #1 kill-shot + #2 Pro/Enterprise screens · `Pricing.md` · v2.1 brief §2.2/§3 (canonical per [[project_setnayan_v2_1_canonical]]) · marketing /pricing + /for-vendors + llms.txt · [Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) (region as the coverage basis; km for transport within region). **Affected files this row:** CLAUDE.md (this row · consolidated model lock). QR Code, Papic, Patiktok, Stories. what else?"* **(1) The model.** **Floor = 100 pax base** (nothing lower — a sub-100 / 50-guest event still pays the 100-pax base for these services; the onboarding keeps the "50" guest chip for *planning + vendor-sizing*, pax-*priced* services just floor at 100) **+ a price per additional 50 pax** above 100 (150 · 200 · 250 · 300 … up to a ceiling, `500+` being the top onboarding chip). The current flat catalog prices become the **100-pax base**; the v2.1 catalog's "up to 250 / up to 300" caps get reframed as base(100) + per-50 increments. **(2) Pax-DEPENDENT services** (cost scales per guest — the test: the service makes/handles something *per guest*): **Custom QR per Guest** (1 QR/guest) · **Papic Guest** (a disposable camera per guest) · **Patiktok** (guest-recorded clips) · **Guest Stories** (a 30-sec story per guest) — the four the owner named — PLUS **Pabati** (guest video-guestbook · "up to 300 videos") · **Papic · 5 Seats** (crew fixed, but guest-media tagging + storage scales) · **High Res Archive** (stores all guest-generated media) · **Indoor Blueprint** (entrance→table seating guide scales with tables/guests). **Borderline (flag):** Live Venue Photo Wall (live collage + count scales with guest contributions) · the **Guided Pack + Media Pack bundles** inherit pax-scaling from whichever pax-dependent services they contain. **(3) FLAT (not pax-dependent)** — one-per-event / audience-independent / per-device / per-vendor: Animated Monogram · Pro Website · Pakanta · Setnayan AI · **Panood** (per-day, audience-independent — YouTube absorbs viewers per the locked Live-Stream decision) · SDE (one video) · Thank You Video (one video) · Live Background (one LED design) · Camera Bridge (per-device) · Call-Time Escalator (scales with vendors, not guests). **(4) Rule of thumb:** pax matters when the output is *per guest* (QR · camera · clip · story · greeting · seat · stored media); it doesn't when the output is *one per event* (monogram · song · one website · one video · one LED loop) or *audience-independent* (livestream). **(5) Open / owner-to-set (NOT invented — pricing guardrail):** the **per-additional-50 increment** per service (+ confirm the current flat price = the 100-pax base) · the **ceiling** behavior at `500+` (flat cap vs keep adding per-50) · **Patiktok** was per-day in an earlier lock but the v2.1 catalog lists it flat ("up to 250 clips") — confirm pax-scaling supersedes the per-day framing · downstream the onboarding "Your Plan" (§3.2) + `/pricing` + the budget compass should eventually show pax-scaled prices for these services. **(6) Tension flagged:** the onboarding offers a 50-pax chip but pax-priced services floor at 100 — consistent by design (50 is for planning/vendor-sizing; the 50-guest couple pays the 100 base on pax-priced services). **Affected files this row:** CLAUDE.md (this row) · NEW memory `project_setnayan_pax_based_pricing.md` (the model + the pax-dependent vs flat classification + open items). | 2026-06-01 | **🎯 Vendor recommendation — inquiry fan-out = 3 (locked) + fair-exposure model + BYO-already-listed → token-activated inquiry · design/spec only · V1.x post-pilot · `Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md` §7b.** Owner: *"okay make it 3"* + *"is it possible that all our vendors in the future will show on the initial vendor recommendations? how do we give chances or opportunity for all vendors to be inquired on?"* + *"if their vendor is already listed and they invited, request will also be sent with activation of tokens."* Three locks. **(1) Inquiry fan-out = 3** (§7b.1). After onboarding, each category's curated top set offers a "send an inquiry to N" action — **default 3, pre-checked, couple-adjustable 1–5**, pre-checked = the top of the fairness-blended rank, **available-only** (only vendors free on the couple's date(s) — candidate-date convergence), explicit send (no auto-send), and the same fan-out re-runs from the dashboard later (onboarding just seeds round one). **(2) Fair exposure — every verified vendor's chance** (§7b.2). The honest answer to "can ALL vendors show on the initial recs": **no, and on purpose** — showing all ~2,400 re-creates the overwhelm the curated top set exists to kill — BUT "curated" must not mean "the entrenched few hoard every lead while new vendors starve," so fairness is engineered in via **7 mechanisms**: (a) **fairness baked into the rank, not a charity slot** — an *exposure-deficit dampener* floats comparable-quality fitting vendors with fewer recent inquiries up so leads **spread** instead of winner-take-all (rises on merit, never forces a weak fit); (b) **new-vendor welcome boost** — a time-boxed cold-start lift (first ~30 days / ~N leads after verification) so 0-review vendors escape the cold-start trap then rank on merit; (c) **reserved rotating "fresh chance" slot** — one shown slot for a rotating fitting newcomer who wouldn't yet make the merit cut (exposure + addable, not auto-pre-checked); (d) **preference diversity** — already in the system, different couples' prefs surface different tops; (e) **Boosted / Sponsored** — the paid self-serve "I want more chances" lever (Tier 3 · token/peso-funded · the revenue engine); (f) **Expand search** — every fitting verified vendor reachable one click away; (g) **direct / by-name inquiry** — any listed vendor is directly inquirable regardless of rank (token-activated). Net: the top stays curated for the couple, but every verified fitting vendor gets a real recurring chance — over time + across couples + on demand + on purchase; none permanently buried, none forced on a couple. Honest vendor-facing framing locked ("you won't always be in a couple's top picks, but you're always reachable, you cycle into the spotlight as leads spread, new vendors get a welcome boost, and you can boost anytime" — NOT "everyone's always on top," which is impossible + dishonest). The specific ranking weights (dampener strength / welcome-boost length / fresh-slot rotation cadence) are a V1.x tuning detail, owner-set on real lead-flow data. **(3) BYO / by-name → token-activated inquiry** (§7b.3). The "Add your own vendor" BYO affordance is **dedup-aware**: if the named vendor is **already listed** (matched by business name / email / phone against existing verified listings), the add+invite becomes a **real inquiry sent to that listing** flowing through the standard token economy — the request reaches the vendor as a lead and **engaging it activates the vendor's tokens** (region-weighted burn, same as any marketplace inquiry · no duplicate cold-invite · the couple is connected to the real listing); if **not on Setnayan**, the cold **`vendor_invites`** flow (claim landing `setnayan.com/vendor/claim/{token}`) → they onboard → verify → then inquiries + tokens flow. This makes BYO/by-name a **first-class discovery channel that bypasses the ranking entirely** — a couple naming a specific vendor is the warmest, highest-intent lead there is, so an existing vendor outside the top set gets a token-activated request the instant the couple wants them by name. The cleanest answer to "how does every vendor get a chance": any listed vendor is directly inquirable, and that inquiry is a paid (token-activated) lead like any other. **Affected files:** `Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md` (new §7b.1/§7b.2/§7b.3 · §11 rows 11–13 [inquiry=3 RESOLVED · fair-exposure model locked · BYO-token RESOLVED] · §12 build item (f)) + its `.docx` mirror · CLAUDE.md (this row). Because that path is anonymous and `/api/upload` 401s anonymous callers, capture runs fully server-side: **`/papic/guest`** reads the cookie → `eventOwnsPapicGuest(admin,...)` → shows the rear camera + remaining credits; **`POST /api/papic/guest-capture`** validates the cookie, PUTs the JPEG to R2 with the service-role client (`r2Upload`, `setnayan-media` bucket, key `papic/guest/{guest_id}/...`), then calls `papic_record_guest_capture` which advisory-locks per guest + atomically re-checks the count + inserts (client display is advisory · the RPC is the gate); a `fetchGuestQuota` pre-check avoids orphaning R2 objects once exhausted. **Reach:** `/[slug]` guest landing — when the couple owns the pack, the cookie-bearing guest gets a floating "Be a candid camera" CTA → `/papic/guest` (gated, admin read, graceful-degrade · the anonymous public landing path untouched; uses the already-imported `admin` client + `Camera`/`Link`). Photos only — 5-sec clips deferred (media bucket MIME image-only). **Same gallery gap as Seats:** guest photos land in R2 → delivered via Photo Delivery → Drive; the in-app real-time gallery (mocked at `Papic_Realtime_Gallery_Preview_2026-06-01.html`) remains the V1.x build. Gates: typecheck 0 · lint clean (new files) · production build 0 (`/papic/guest` + `/api/papic/guest-capture` compile). No migration in this PR — table + RPC already live on prod. Affected: NEW `apps/web/app/papic/guest/{page.tsx,_components/papic-guest-capture.tsx}` · NEW `apps/web/app/api/papic/guest-capture/route.ts` · `apps/web/lib/v2-catalog.ts` (PAPIC_GUEST → live) · `apps/web/app/[slug]/page.tsx` (guest CTA). | 2026-06-02 | **📸 Papic vs Once.film competitive benchmark + per-pax pricing framework + a confirmed PRICE DRIFT to reconcile (analysis only · no code/migration this row).** Owner ran a competitive review of **Once** (once.film · App Store id6754265953 · by 10xCompany · 4.8★/282 ratings · iOS/iPad/Mac/visionOS) — the closest direct competitor to Papic's guest-camera slice. **(1) Once's exact pricing** (one-time per event · free ≤5 participants · App Clip, no guest download): 10 pax $1.99 (~₱110) · 25 $4.99 (~₱280) · 50 $14.99 (~₱840) · 100 $29.99 (~₱1,680) · 150 $49.99 (~₱2,800) · 200 $69.99 (~₱3,920) · Unlimited $99.99 (~₱5,600) [≈₱56/$, approx]. Effective per-pax ≈ **₱11–20/pax flat** ("cheaper than a disposable camera per guest"). **(2) Once's full feature set:** photos only (**NO video**), configurable/unlimited shots, film-look filter (server-rendered, skin-tone-accurate), delayed-reveal-default OR instant, recap video, participants list with **who-shot-it attribution** (NOT who's-IN-it tagging), Once-watermark + timezone, push notifications, multi-event, private host-controlled gallery, mobile-web album, full download, photos never expire. **(3) Verdict — Papic wins where it matters, on BOTH price and capability:** at PH wedding scale (150–300 guests) Once lands at its ~₱3,920–₱5,600 tiers while Papic is cheaper AND a superset — video clips, **guest tagging (QR + table-QR + face-detect auto-tag) → per-guest tagged delivery** (Once has none of this · the single biggest gap), real-time delivery to the couple's landing page, 1–30s personal souvenir reels, custom monogram, Drive-to-own-storage, NSFW filter, geo/EXIF, offline queue, paparazzi seats, platform integration. Once only undercuts on sticker at ≤100-guest events (not the core market) for a strictly lesser product. Where Once is genuinely ahead: it **ships native + polished today** (App Clip · per-photo film look) while Papic V1 is web-first (native is already roadmapped V1.5+ per iteration 0052 — no change needed). **(4) Per-pax pricing framework (RECOMMENDED · owner-to-set final · NOT migrated):** keep the locked ₱2,999 floor (100 pax) + set the per-50 increment at **~₱450** ("School A · cheaper-AND-better") → effective per-pax glides ₱30 (at 100) → ₱16 (at 300), staying at/under Once across 150–300 while out-delivering it; the declining curve rewards big weddings (where Once gets priciest). COGS is near-zero (R2 egress free · storage pennies · face-detect on-device) so margin ~85–95% across the curve — the increment is a positioning lever, not cost recovery. School B (value-premium ~₱600–800/50, sit above Once) is the alternative; owner's stated instinct favors A. Couple-facing frame: "every guest a candid camera for ~₱20/head" = 0.2–0.6% of the ₱3,500–10,000/head PH wedding budget. **(5) ⚠️ CONFIRMED DRIFT (the real action item):** the live `platform_retail_catalog_v2` ships **PAPIC_GUEST ₱2,999 + PAPIC_SEATS ₱2,999, both FLAT** (seeded `20260628000000_v2_additive_phase_a.sql` · no later migration re-prices them · verified in `~/setnayan-db-push`, which may be slightly behind origin/main — confirm there). | 2026-06-02 | **🗓️ Schedule Matrix & Date Finder — date-from-vendor-availability convergence + capacity-aware blocking + honest 3-tier "eyeing" signal LOCKED · design/spec only · V1.x post-pilot · canonical doc [Schedule_Matrix_and_Date_Finder_2026-06-02.md](03_Strategy/Schedule_Matrix_and_Date_Finder_2026-06-02.md).** Owner: *"i need a way for us to end up with specific dates based on the vendors ... we check the available schedule of vendors. if they are available, for any of those schedules, we add them. Then we want to know what combination of vendors would be available for this schedule, and that schedule"* + *"we also want to update the customer if someone is eyeing on their schedule right now."* Makes concrete the candidate-set date-resolution design ([Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md](03_Strategy/Vendor_Match_Personalization_2026-06-01.md) §2) and adds the capacity + honesty refinements. **(1) The date is an OUTPUT.** The couple gives candidate dates (specific list or a window) + the vendors they want; the system returns which date keeps the most of those vendors available — a matrix (candidate dates across, shortlisted vendors down, a tick where the vendor is open) with a recommended date + the trade-offs. **Shortlist by UNION** (a vendor qualifies if free on ≥1 candidate date — "if available for any of those schedules, we add them"), **converge by INTERSECTION** (each candidate date yields a feasible vendor combination; pick the best column). One shared engine — candidate-date overlap — powers BOTH the matrix AND the eyeing signal; extends `apps/web/lib/vendor-availability.ts` (already computes per-vendor free days + the locked-vendor intersection the /vendors marketplace uses today). **(2) THREE availability states, not two** — confirmed-free / no-conflicts-on-file / busy. Never call a no-data vendor "free" (say "no conflicts on file — confirm with vendor"); keeps empty calendars honest while vendors fill them. **(3) Capacity-aware blocking (owner refinement this row).** A date is NOT blocked the moment someone pays — it is blocked when the vendor runs out of slots that day. NEW column `vendor_profiles.daily_booking_capacity` (INT default 1; most wedding vendors 1, caterer/HMUA-team 2-3). Each paid booking (`deposit_paid`) uses one slot; the date flips to Busy only when the last slot is gone; limit 2 + 1 booking = still open → surface "1 slot left." Busy if paid bookings ≥ capacity OR a manual full-day block exists. `daily_booking_capacity` is the delivery limit; the existing `max_soft_holds_per_date` stays the separate tentative-hold fairness cap. **(4) Calendars fill layered, cheapest-truth-first** — auto-decrement-on-deposit (do first · zero vendor effort · the deferred Rule 5 made capacity-aware) → a vendor "blocked dates" screen (off-platform bookings + days off) → Google/Apple sync (V1.5+). **(5) Soft-hold timing — Option A locked.** Shortlisting places NO hold; a soft-hold fires only when the couple narrows to one date and locks → keeps the per-(vendor,date) fairness cap honest, no couple ties up a vendor across 4 tentative dates. **(6) Honest "eyeing" signal — 3 tiers, all real + aggregate + overlapping-dates-scoped.** Considering (another couple inquired about the same vendor with overlapping candidate dates) → Held (a real soft-hold at lock) → Booked (a competitor downpayment → "slot gone, here are 3 alternatives"). STARTS AT THE INQUIRY (Stage 2), NEVER at search appearance (Stage 1): appearing in a couple's search results is an impression not intent, and counting it = manufactured scarcity, a fineable dark pattern. Fires synchronously on the real inquiry (no cron) → notifies the other couples chasing that vendor+date (in-app + an optional 0028 email), throttled (one nudge per genuine event · max ~1/day per vendor-date). **(7) Privacy (RA 10173) — rules at every tier:** aggregate counts only (never identities) · never cross-leak the other side's plans (each side sees a count, not the other party's list) · suppress at small N (a bare "1" on a niche vendor + specific date + small area re-identifies one real person — don't show it / strip the pinpoint specificity). The privacy failure mode (naming/cross-leak) is SEPARATE from the honesty failure mode (Stage-1 search as intent); with both held there is no privacy conflict. **(8) Build order — keystone first:** (a) onboarding Phase-4 commit writes `events.date_candidates/date_window/date_mode` — KEYSTONE, the same fix also closes the onboarding→home personalization gap; Phase 2 already ships the date-picker UI (PR #762), the missing piece is the DB commit → (b) `daily_booking_capacity` + auto-decrement-on-deposit + vendor blocked-dates screen → (c) the shared engine + 3-state availability → (d) "Find your date" surface + date commit → (e) the honest eyeing notification + 0028 template + escalation + throttle. **Schema/cross-iteration:** `events` date columns (schema'd in migration 20260719000000, need the onboarding write) · `vendor_profiles.daily_booking_capacity` (NEW) · `vendor_calendar_blocks` (exists, manual/synced day-off blocks) · `event_vendors`/`orders` (paid-booking source + the inquiry/hold/booked tiers) · 0028 (new email templates) · owning iterations 0006 + 0021 + 0016/0043 + 0028 + 0034. Now `.select('event_id')` + threads the UUID through `event_members.event_id` + `captureEvent` + the return — matching the canonical `createWeddingEvent` (`dashboard/create-event/actions.ts`). This is the bug that would have broken the entire Phase-5 cutover on first use. **(2) 🏛️ `venue_setting` DERIVED from the reception pick.** New `RECEPTION_TO_VENUE_SETTING` map: the couple's first reception "setting" pick (screen-10 · `setting_ballroom`/`events_place`/`restaurant`→`banquet_hall` · `setting_heritage`→`heritage` · `setting_garden`→`garden` · `setting_beach`→`beach` · `setting_resort`→`destination`) seeds `events.venue_setting` instead of the blind `banquet_hall` default → the marketplace reception filter (PR #311 `?venue=`) is correct out of the gate. Falls back to `banquet_hall` (the CHECK-constraint-required value for weddings) when no setting was picked. **(3) 📨 Auto-inquire best-fit per picked category** (owner AskUserQuestion answer: "Auto-inquire best-fit per category"). New `PICK_TO_GROUP` map resolves the 53 screen-9 picker keys → **unique** PLAN_GROUP ids; the commit then fires `unlockCategoryWithInquiry({eventId, groupId})` (the dashboard unlock-category flow from PR #774: best-fit pick via the 6-tier ladder → `event_vendors` 'considering' → `followVendor` → `chat_threads` upsert → first `chat_messages` inquiry firing `vendor_inquiry_received`) per group, **`Promise.allSettled` (best-effort + parallel)** so an inquiry failure NEVER fails the commit (the `events` + `event_members` rows are already saved · the event_members row is committed BEFORE the loop so `unlockCategoryWithInquiry`'s user-scoped RLS membership read resolves). Picks with no clean planning group are **intentionally omitted** (`fireworks`/`outdoor`/`livestream`/`editorial`/`wellness`/`escort` + the niche booths beyond `cocktail_booths`+`photobooth`) so a pick can never fire a wrong-category inquiry — the couple adds those from the dashboard Unlock-categories page (same by-design limitation per PR #774). Picks land as a real shortlist + inbox → the data the Personalization page (Phase B) documents + edits. **State wiring** (`apps/web/app/onboarding/wedding/_components/onboarding-shell.tsx`): `buildCommitPayload` now passes `picks: s.picks` + `receptionSettings: s.prefs.reception`; `OnboardingCommitPayload` gained `picks: string[]` + `receptionSettings: string[]`. **DEFERRED to Phase A2:** the screen-10 STYLE prefs (cuisine / ceremony-where / pv-look / dietary) → `event_vendor_preferences` — that table's `canonical_service` FK must be verified against `canonical_service_schemas` (FOUNDATION-ONLY/unread per CLAUDE.md 2026-06-02 · high FK-violation risk if guessed) before writing; `mood_feel_key` + `music_playlist_seed` already persist as `events` columns. **Scope:** 2 files · no new surface (the commit path) · **no migration** (the 12 v2 columns shipped in `20260719000000`; `event_vendors`/`chat_threads`/`chat_messages` already live). | 2026-06-02 | **🗓️💰 Service Schedule & Quotation Flow — design LOCKED (7 owner decisions) · canonical doc [Service_Schedule_and_Quotation_Flow_2026-06-02.md](03_Strategy/Service_Schedule_and_Quotation_Flow_2026-06-02.md) · V1.x post-pilot · design lock only (no code/migration/SKU/pricing).** Owner walked the full customer ⇄ service ⇄ vendor schedule + pricing lifecycle and answered the 7 forks I surfaced; this row + the canonical doc lock it. **The 7 decisions:** **(1)** A date is "taken" at **vendor-approved-lock — NOT at payment** ("they already agreed to terms · we do not need to check if they paid · it boils down to how they observe each other") → commitment is a Setnayan-observable, vendor-controlled signal, NOT off-platform self-reported money. **(2)** A lock request **stays pending + nudges the vendor, 48h ceiling**; no auto-approve; at 48h unactioned → **auto-expires** (customer freed, never stranded). **(3)** *(the strongest new rule)* whoever the vendor approves wins, **but a vendor cannot approve a lock while competing requests are pending — they must explicitly DECLINE the others first** ("a proper and respectful way to make sure no customer just loses the lock with no reason") → a loss is always a deliberate, acknowledged decline, never a silent slot-fill; multi-slot vendor declines everyone beyond who they're taking. **(4)** **Schedule is the hard gate** — a service "will not show unless a schedule is mutual" → locked as: hide only when **confirmed-busy on ALL the customer's candidate dates**; an **unfilled calendar = possibly-mutual → still shows** ("availability to confirm", else cold-start hides everyone); the DATE filter is a true hide (NOT Expand search) while area/pax/faith/cert still route to Expand per Vendor_Match §7 · owner can override to strict-confirmed-only (§6 flag b). **(5)** **Customer requests, vendor approves; they chat first, then the vendor issues a quotation tailored to the specific request** → confirms the structured vendor-issued quotation as a V1.x build (owner-approved feature expansion). **(6)** **Reveal happens right after the vendor pays the booking-request token** (token-payment is the reveal trigger, before any message). **(7)** **Setnayan only provides tools to navigate together — it has no means to check payment** → vendor↔customer money is off-platform + untracked-as-truth; "payment status" is what they record/observe, not a Setnayan-verified state. **Architectural consequence — scheduling-commit + payment DECOUPLED:** no-overlap is handled entirely by vendor-approved-lock (Setnayan-observable); payment is a shared tracking/coordination tool (vendor-set milestone deadlines + ledger), entirely off-platform, Setnayan only displays — more robust than the old deposit-tied model since under 0% publisher Setnayan can't see off-platform self-reported money. Two payment realities on the dashboard kept unambiguous: (a) external vendor services = tracked-only/off-platform/customer-approves-the-figure (this lock) · (b) Setnayan Productions SKUs (Papic/Panood/…) = real Setnayan checkout. **The flow as 2 state machines.** **Track 1 SCHEDULE (no-overlap):** discovery (≥1 mutual date) → booking-request/inquiry (auto-populates vendor calendar, informational) → vendor Accept + **pay token** → **whitelist** (accepted-pending · informational · does NOT block the date) + chat opens + names reveal → customer **lock request** (≤48h pending) → vendor **approve** (after declining competitors) = **Confirmed** → slot consumed (capacity via `daily_booking_capacity`, blocks date when slots run out). **Track 2 PRICE (vendor-issued quotation):** 1 main photo + ≤5 photos + line items (service cost · transportation · food allowance · additional costs w/ description, addable anytime) + per-row service details + linked cross-category services (each priced + described, respects saturation + package-inclusion auto-tag) + **vendor-set payment deadlines**; **every change timestamped + versioned**; **any price change needs the customer's approval** (tracking-layer acknowledgement, NOT a payment authorization) before the new version is the active agreement; line items map to the 0007 3-line budget (Package=service cost · Crew Meal=food allowance · Transportation). The **service page** surfaces the active quotation + payment status + schedule state + change history. **What this SUPERSEDES/RECONCILES:** supersedes "capacity decrements on `deposit_paid`" (Schedule Matrix §2) + **lock/delete/overlap Rule 4** (auto-release on downpayment) → slot consumes at vendor-approved-lock · reframes the **soft-hold Option A** (the customer's "lock" becomes a vendor-arbitrated **lock request**; adds the **whitelist** accepted-pending state between inquiry and lock) · overrides Vendor_Match "all hard filters → Expand" **for the date dimension only** (date-mutual is a hard prerequisite to appear) · confirms the **structured vendor-issued quotation** as a new V1.x object superseding the loose 0006 `package + inclusions + couple-encoded milestones` (authorship flips couple→vendor; becomes versioned + customer-approved) · **refines hybrid-anonymity** [[project_setnayan_vendor_hybrid_anonymity]] — reveal trigger moves from "first vendor chat reply" → **"vendor pays the booking-request token"** (venue exception + Pro+-always-shown still hold; memory updated) · **reconciles the shipped auto-inquiry** (PR #774/#783) — today it opens a chat immediately with no Accept/Decline + no token (the pilot simplification); under this lock it becomes "booking request sent → vendor Accept/Decline → on Accept + token-pay → chat opens + reveal" (the shipped immediate-chat becomes a "pending vendor accept" state). **Schema (design-level, no migration):** `inquiry_state` enum (`requested`/`accepted`/`lock_requested`/`confirmed`/`declined`/`expired`) + `token_paid_at`(=`revealed_at`) + `lock_requested_at`/`lock_expires_at`(=+48h)/`confirmed_at`/`declined_at`/`decline_reason` on the relationship · whitelist = derived (`accepted` rows grouped by vendor+date, informational, never blocks) · `daily_booking_capacity` (Schedule Matrix · slot consumed at `confirmed`, not payment) · NEW `vendor_quotations` (main_photo + photos[] + version + customer_approval_state) + `vendor_quotation_lines` (kind ∈ service_cost/transportation/food_allowance/additional/service_detail/linked_category · linked_canonical_service · label/description/amount_centavos) · `vendor_payment_milestones` authorship flipped couple→vendor, attached to the quotation, tracking-only. **4 small sub-decisions flagged (§6):** (a) decline-reason mandatory vs optional → lean **optional** · (b) unfilled-calendar show-vs-strict → lean **show** · (c) old quotation version stays active until the new is approved → **yes** · (d) declined slot reopens to a new whitelist → **yes**. **Build order (V1.x):** engagement state machine + token-on-accept + reveal-on-token → whitelist (vendor dashboard) → lock-request + 48h pending + decline-others-first + auto-expire + slot-consume-on-confirmed → date-as-hard-gate discovery → vendor quotation (issue/version/lines/cross-category/customer-approval/deadlines) → service page → 0028 emails (Accept/Decline nudge · 48h lock-request nudge · decline notice · quotation-issued · price-change-approval-needed · no-longer-available). Depends on the Schedule Matrix capacity work + the token economy + the Vendor_Match verification gate landing first. **Owning iterations (per-iteration .md edits QUEUED for next Cowork sync pass per | 2026-06-03 | **⌨🔁 Guests rapid-add — re-focus First name after Enter on last name FIXED (PR [#839](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/839) merged).** Owner-reported: *"after i pressed enter on last name. it did not return to first name."* Latent focus bug in the mobile rapid-add loop (`QuickAddInlineForm.addGuest` in `mobile-guest-carousel.tsx` · the loop emphasized by PR #824). **Root cause:** the success path called `firstRef.current?.focus()` **synchronously** right after the `await` — but the inputs are `disabled={busy}`, `busy` is set `true` BEFORE the await and only reset to `false` in the `finally` (which hadn't run yet), so at the focus call the field was **still disabled**, and `focus()` is a **no-op on a disabled element**. The per-guest add + field-clear always worked; only the loop-back focus was silently lost. **Fix (1 line):** defer the focus a tick — `firstRef.current?.focus()` → `setTimeout(() => firstRef.current?.focus(), 0)` — so it lands AFTER React flushes `busy=false` and re-enables the field. Mirrors the deferred-focus pattern (`setTimeout(… focus, 0)`) the sibling `QuickAddSheet` already uses after its async adds. **Mobile-only · single line · no schema/route/migration/SKU change.** Type-safe by inspection (sync call → `setTimeout` arrow); heavy gates (`typecheck + lint` · `production build`) verified post-merge (this repo's auto-merge fires on the fast checks; heavy ones run after — background-polled green). Per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] PR #839 auto-merged on green · per [[feedback_setnayan_push_migrations_myself]] N/A · per [[feedback_setnayan_button_preservation]] the rapid-add two-input loop + Enter handlers preserved verbatim — only the focus timing fixed · per [[feedback_setnayan_document_changes_with_why]] WHY in commit/PR + this row. **Cross-references:** the 2026-06-03 "⏎ Guests rapid-add loops FOREVER (PR #824)" row (the loop this restores the cursor for) · the sibling `QuickAddSheet` (the `setTimeout(0)` re-focus precedent) · iteration [0001 Guest List](0001_creating_guest_list/0001_creating_guest_list.md). **Sequencing note.** Live-route bugfix · 1 PR merged · pilot 2026-06-01 production · no migration · no SKU change · no V1 scope expansion. `.docx` mirror deferred per convention. |

| 2026-06-03 | **⌨️📌 Guests Add/Search sheet PINNED above the iOS keyboard (PR [#841](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/841) merged).** Owner-reported (screenshot · iOS Safari): when the keyboard opens on the mobile Guests carousel Add panel, the whole `position:fixed` sheet floats up into the MIDDLE of the screen with dead space + the bottom nav still eats a row — instead of the two textboxes sitting right above the keyboard. *"we don't want the whole screen to go up … what we will only see from bottom is keyboard then the two textboxes and the guest list."* **Root cause:** iOS Safari keeps the LAYOUT viewport full-height and shrinks the VISUAL viewport when the keyboard opens, so a fixed bottom sheet is mispositioned (and iOS auto-scrolls the page to reveal the focused input). **Fix (`mobile-guest-carousel.tsx`, 1 file):** new **`useKeyboardInset()`** hook reads `window.visualViewport` (`gap = window.innerHeight − vv.height − vv.offsetTop` = keyboard+accessory-bar height, rAF-debounced, `resize`+`scroll` listeners, feature-detected `if (!vv) return`). When `kbInset > 100` (real keyboard, ignores Safari-toolbar jitter): (1) **pin the sheet flush above the keyboard** via inline `style={{ bottom: kbInset }}`; (2) **on the Add panel** (`active === 2`) **shrink the sheet to 190px** (~the two inputs) so the guest list above keeps the reclaimed space — other panels keep `--gcar-h` so Search isn't clipped (it scrolls); (3) **hide the bottom nav** (`${kbOpen ? 'hidden' : ''}`) since it'd only sit behind the keyboard. Result bottom-to-top: **keyboard → two textboxes → guest list.** Closed-keyboard layout unchanged (inline `style` is `undefined` → the Tailwind classes apply); desktop unaffected (carousel `lg:hidden`, `kbInset` stays 0). **Mobile-only · single file · no schema/route/migration/SKU change.** Type-safe (VisualViewport narrowed by the null-guard; style values are valid numbers; no inline JSX comments — moved rationale to the component body to avoid any parse risk since the `/tmp` worktree can't typecheck); heavy gates (`typecheck + lint` · `production build`) background-verified post-merge (repo auto-merges on the fast checks · CI queue was badly backed up today). **Flagged for owner device verification** (visual-viewport keyboard math can't be exercised headlessly · PR checklist). | 2026-06-07 | **🪙 Vendor token economy CONNECTED — burn-on-answer + strict free-tokens/anti-merge + login-driven ghosting (owner "connect the tokens properly" + 2 refinements · setnayan-platform PR #1057 MERGED + PR #1059).** The vendor token economy was **economically inert** — `unlock-category.ts` literally said the burn "is NOT wired yet," so vendors answered inquiries free. Wired the owner-locked (2026-06-05) **burn-on-answer**: accepting an inquiry IS the answer (the accept-gate means a vendor can't even reply before accepting), and it costs **ONE idempotent unlock per (vendor_profile_id, event_id)** that covers **ALL** the vendor's services for that event. To-scale tables are intentionally small (correct); the couple zooms in (now-smooth pan) to seat. tsc/lint/build clean; repro-verified (20×30 room, all tables + stage + entrance visible in capped canvas). | 2026-06-09 | **🔥 HOT-DATE "heat" demand layer defined + folded into the Date Aligner (corpus draft · not yet built).** The onboarding/calendar date picker gets a **demand readout parallel to the fit ranker**: every date carries a heat color (transparent→red) + a **1–4 flame count** with a tap-nugget. **Definition for the spec:** a date is **"hot" when its demand sub-score reaches the In-demand tier (≥ tier 3 of 4).** Two confidence-blended sources: **(L.1) predicted / deterministic** — peak-month × Saturday × repeating-number × Valentine's/long-weekend; cold-start-safe, zero-volume = a *forecast* ("history says this books out"); and **(L.2) observed = Setnayan's own internal app statistics** (owner addition this session): # couples targeting the date (`date_candidates`/`date_window`/`events.event_date`) + **inquiry pressure** (`chat_threads`+`event_vendors`, funnel-weighted eyeing<inquired<downpayment<booked) + **vendor fill %** (`vendor_calendar_blocks`+capacity). **The demand headcount ESCALATES the tier, RELATIVE TO SUPPLY** (core mechanic · owner chose relative-to-supply over flat-count 2026-06-09): `pressure = contested_couples / available_vendors_that_day` (in-region · at the BOTTLENECK category) → `pressure_boost` (admin bands, illustrative `<25%→+0 · 25–49%→+1 · 50–74%→+2 · 75–99%→+3 · ≥100%→cap Hottest`) → `tier = min(Hottest, predicted_tier + pressure_boost)`. *More couples chasing the same free vendors = hotter,* and it can lift a plain weekday **past its forecast** (real scarcity). **Why relative not "every-10":** 10 inquiries vs 100 vendors = nothing · 10 vs 8 = sell-out — the RATIO auto-scales cold-start→full marketplace, no magic count to re-tune. Floors: **min-N couples AND min-supply** before trusting the ratio (else 1 vendor+1 inquiry≠Hottest → fall back to forecast w/ low-confidence label). Nugget above min-N: "👀 N couples chasing the M vendors free that day (X% booked-pressure)". *(Retires the absolute-count band proposal.)* **Guardrails:** min-N suppression (observed contributes nothing below an admin-set N — statistical honesty + RA 10173 small-N) · aggregate + de-identified, couple sees color never *who* (behavioral-data = top-protection moat) · self-reinforcement caution (surfacing hot biases stats → scarcity/hidden-gem logic keys off **vendor availability**, not couple-interest alone) · admin kill-switch. Hot is **information, never a verdict** (a hot date can be the top pick OR be down-ranked under Least-stressful for crowding+premium). All thresholds (month weights · tier cutoffs · min-N · %-fill cutoff · predicted↔observed blend) are **owner-to-set** admin reference tables (Aligner §J.1). Demand feeds D4 surge framing — not a new engine. **Prototype:** `Hot_Date_Heat_Calendar_Prototype_2026-06-09.html` (single + range/flexible modes · two-axis demand+fit nugget · verified in preview). | Owner: "how many people inquiring a date must also score the hot date." | 2026-06-14 | **🔁 SERVICE-WORKER CACHE VERSION NOW AUTO-STAMPS PER DEPLOY — durable fix for "returning PWA users get the prior build's stale shell" (the chrome-retirement follow-up; was a one-time manual v3→v4 bump) [PR #1403].** `public/sw.js` namespaces all 5 caches (SHELL/STATIC/IMAGE/FONT/DAYOF) by a hand-maintained `const VERSION`; `STATIC_CACHE` is stale-while-revalidate over Next chunks, so an un-bumped VERSION strands returning users on the old shell for one load. New `apps/web/scripts/stamp-sw.mjs` rewrites the `const VERSION='…'` line to `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (12-char) at build — wired into `apps/web` `package.json` "build" (`node scripts/stamp-sw.mjs && next build`) AND `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` added to `turbo.json` build `env` (forces a per-commit cache MISS so the stamp ALWAYS runs — without it a revert/redeploy/root-only commit could turbo-cache-hit and skip the stamp, recurring the bug; caught in adversarial review). Mechanism: every deploy → sw.js bytes change → browser SW-update check re-fetches `/sw.js` (already `no-cache` per next.config) → byte-diff → installs new worker → existing `install`(skipWaiting)+`activate`(delete non-KNOWN_CACHES + clients.claim) evict the prior caches. Registration stays `/sw.js` (a `?v=<sha>` URL is defeated by the stale shell re-registering the old URL — file-byte-change on a fixed URL is the reliable trigger). Regex is line-anchored (`/^const VERSION = '…';/m`) so it hits ONLY the code line, fails the build if the line vanishes, and no-ops (keeps `'v4'`) when the SHA is unset (dev/local never dirties the file). Stamp unit-tested; adversarial-reviewed (2 wiring fixes applied). **OWNER QA:** Capacitor WebView (`apps/mobile`) uses the same SW+no-cache path → propagates by design; confirm with one Android + one iOS deploy-then-reopen. | 2026-06-14 | **HOMEPAGE hero scrub: repeat-visit browser caching on the presigned path (perf follow-up to #1426).** Owner: "always checking on the first visit, but yes we also cache it for the repeated visits." First-visit = progressive release (#1426); this makes a RETURNING visitor re-use browser-cached frames instead of re-downloading tens of MB. On the live presigned path (R2 S3 endpoint, no public host) two things blocked caching: the signed URL was re-minted every 6h (cache-key churn) + the GET carried no Cache-Control. FIX: (1) `r2SignedGet` gains optional `responseCacheControl` → signs the S3 `response-cache-control` override into the URL so R2 returns it on GET (no re-upload); (2) hero frames request `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (keys are content-stable — republish writes NEW keys); (3) presign lifetime 24h→7d (SigV4 max), re-sign interval 6h→6d → same signed URL served ~6 days → browser cache key stops churning (republish still bumps `updated_at`→fresh URLs). Returning-visitor re-download drops from "every 6h/maybe every visit" → "≤ once per ~6 days." BEST end-state (edge/CDN cache + permanently stable URLs) = owner binds the media bucket to a PUBLIC HOST + points `R2_PUBLIC_URL` at it; read path (`resolveMediaUrls`/`publicHostConfigured`) ALREADY auto-switches to public URLs — Cloudflare config only, no further code. | 2026-06-15 | **BROWSER ZOOM DISABLED APP-WIDE → native-app feel; seat-plan canvas excepted** (owner: "we do not want this to zoom. we want zoom disabled on the whole app except for the seat-plan touch/drag area"). Reverses the prior "deliberate pinch-zoom stays ENABLED for WCAG 1.4.4" stance. Mechanism = **two layers**: (1) viewport meta `maximumScale: 1` + `userScalable: false` (kills Android Chrome pinch + the iOS **input focus-zoom** — the auto-zoom on tapping a sub-16px field, which was the original login complaint); (2) NEW `<ZoomGuard/>` client component preventing WebKit `gesturestart`/`gesturechange`/`gestureend` at the document level, because **iOS Safari deliberately IGNORES the viewport meta for the user's pinch gesture** (accessibility) — preventing gesture\* stops pinch WITHOUT touching scroll (they fire only for pinch/rotate). The **seat-plan editor canvas** carries `data-allow-zoom` so its own pointer-event pan/pinch (on a `touch-none` canvas) is exempt; ZoomGuard skips any `[data-allow-zoom]` subtree. Scope = **touch pinch only**; desktop keyboard (⌘/Ctrl ±/0) + trackpad (ctrl+wheel) browser zoom intentionally left alone. ⚠ **Accessibility:** trades away WCAG 1.4.4 browser pinch-zoom by explicit owner decision; OS-level Accessibility→Zoom remains the fallback. Carries the 16px input-floor `!important` fix (same PR) as defense-in-depth. Guest-facing seat views (`/[slug]/find-seat`, seating `walkthrough`) NOT carved out — editor only, per "touch/drag area"; revisit if guest pinch wanted.
