Root cause: the new `/onboarding/wedding` flow drives its 15+ screens with pure React state (`go(d)`), so the on-screen "‹" worked but the **device hardware Back / browser Back / mobile swipe-back were never intercepted** — they popped the page out of onboarding to whatever loaded before it; for the dashboard→`create-event`→Wedding entry path that previous page was the legacy `/dashboard/create-event` event-type picker = the "old onboarding". Removed the per-page `<Nav>` (import+render) from all 12 pages (home/about/how-it-works/pricing/for-vendors/our-story/blog/realstories/features/explore/tl·about/tl·how-it-works). Core: sealing wax = thermoplastic (melt ~71–82°C), whole craft = hitting ONE viscosity window. Process: melt-slowly(don't overheat→bubbles) → pour runny puddle (self-levels into a bead, size=amount) → COOL ~10s to "soft but not runny" (the make-or-break) → chill/moisten stamp (anti-stick) → press STRAIGHT down firmly, NEVER twist (deboss field + emboss design + edge bulge) → hold 30s+ then lift straight/rock, never twist. THE refinement for our sim: a THREE-zone consistency window (too-liquid=smear/flow-back · soft-set=CRISP reward · too-hard=shallow/won't-take), not the 2-zone we had; plus ~10–20s timing, no-twist release smear, overheat→bubbles. Fix: (1) give the disc a TAPERED, rounded edge (smoothstep meniscus over the outer ~0.11 band) instead of a vertical cliff — also more physically correct (real wax has a meniscus); (2) ALPHA-TO-COVERAGE soft alpha at the edge (MSAA coverage) on top of supersampling → the thin tapered rim antialiases to a smooth curve. Build rule: never cut a cutout/discard mesh at a hard grid-rasterized boundary — taper it + use alphaToCoverage/supersample. Prototype: wax_creation_smooth_rim. | 0024_save_the_date/0024_ADDENDUM_envelope_open_experience_2026-06-14.md §3 |

Fix: the press now only DEFORMS EXISTING WAX (skip cells with no wax) — flattens the contact area into the blob + bulges displaced wax outward, so the seal stays ONE CONTINUOUS organic blob with the couple's drip outline (no disc, no slice); monogram embosses via the field bump. Added STAMP SIZE slider (rs ~0.24–0.56, default small) + the visual stamp mesh scales to match. Build rule: a seal press is a deformation of the existing wax body, never a circle drawn independent of it. | 2026-06-16 | Save-the-Date · PREVIEW STRATEGY settled (owner reasoning). Preview is PERSONALIZED (the couple's real monogram/names/date/palette/reveal), NOT a generic non-them sample — informed buyers convert more + refund less ("no this-isn't-what-I-expected"); a generic sample forces a leap of faith + under-sells. RISK = screen recording → REFRAME: you can't stop screen capture, so make the CAPTURE WORTHLESS, not impossible. Mitigation = centred SETNAYAN watermark (over design + video) + reduced resolution → a grab is a branded blurry thumbnail, not a sendable Save the Date. ⚠ CAUTION on "make it really small to maximize": over-correction — the preview's JOB is to SELL, so DON'T over-shrink; the WATERMARK is the lock, not tininess. Keep it GENEROUSLY VIEWABLE (big enough to fall in love with); protect via watermark + low-res, not size. Defense-in-depth extras: DEAD/placeholder QR in preview (no working RSVP link), no download/right-click, video-in-preview = short watermarked LOOP not the full film. Rule: personalized · centred watermark · lower-res · generously sized to seduce · dead QR · clean full version on UNLOCK. Refines the prior watermark-preview row. | 0024_save_the_date/0024_ADDENDUM_envelope_open_experience_2026-06-14.md §7 |
| 2026-06-16 | Save-the-Date · preview DOWNLOAD-protection = a 3-LAYER STACK (owner Q: "if they download the photo, the watermark is on top, so only the watermark downloads?"). YES that works (for <img>): a transparent WATERMARK OVERLAY on top → right-click "Save image" grabs the topmost image (the watermark), not the design beneath (stock-photo trick); the design rendered as DOM/CSS/SVG has no "save image" target at all. LIMITS (honest): the overlay does NOT stop SCREENSHOTS / screen-recording, and for the live reveal (a CANVAS) "save image" = canvas pixels → the watermark must be BAKED INTO the render, not overlaid. So layer it: (1) transparent watermark overlay (beats casual save) → (2) preview render is LOW-RES with watermark BAKED IN (screenshots capture only a branded/blurry, unusable frame) → (3) THE REAL LOCK: the clean full-res master is NEVER SENT to the browser — not in the DOM/network/right-click; generated + served ONLY after UNLOCK via a short-lived SIGNED URL. Do all three → capture is pointless, nothing worth taking. Visual: preview_protection_stack. | 0024_save_the_date/0024_ADDENDUM_envelope_open_experience_2026-06-14.md §7 |
| 2026-06-16 | Save-the-Date · "protect from inspect element" — STANCE (owner request). HONEST: you CANNOT block inspect/DevTools (it's the user's browser); disabling right-click/F12 + devtools-detection are trivially bypassed, hostile to power users, and harm accessibility → DO NOT rely on them (theatre). REFRAME: make inspecting BORING — the page must contain NO secret to find. Guarantees: (1) the served preview <img> IS ALREADY the watermarked LOW-RES derivative (watermark baked into the FILE, not a removable overlay div) → peeling the overlay in DevTools reveals the same watermarked low-res, no clean layer behind it; (2) every media URL is a SHORT-LIVED SIGNED link (session-tied) → copying it from the network tab is useless/expired; (3) the reveal is a <canvas> (no source image to grab; watermark painted into pixels → at most a watermarked screenshot); (4) THE REAL LOCK: clean full-res master is NEVER sent to the browser (not DOM/network/right-click) — generated server-side + served ONLY post-unlock via the signed link. Optional hardeners: FORENSIC watermark (stamp the couple's account-id invisibly → leak traceability) + for the SD VIDEO, encrypted/segmented HLS streaming (no single downloadable .mp4). Extends the preview_protection_stack. | 0024_save_the_date/0024_ADDENDUM_envelope_open_experience_2026-06-14.md §7 |

| 2026-06-16 | **NATIVE APP → PAY ON THE WEBSITE (BDO/GCash, base price) — owner "website is cheaper · website charges via BDO and GCash" (AskUserQuestion: "Send them to the website"). SUPERSEDES the +30% native markup (#1458 CLOSED).** The reality: the app is a Capacitor web-wrapper using the SAME BDO/GCash checkout — there is no IAP in code. So the +30% would have been charged via BDO/GCash in-app = an overcharge (no store cut to cover) AND Apple/Google forbid selling digital goods in-app via an external rail (App Store rejection). RESOLUTION: the app routes payment OUT to the website. `InlineCheckoutDrawer` detects the native shell post-mount (`SetnayanApp` UA, same marker as middleware `isCapacitorClient`) and on native the buy trigger opens the checkout page in the EXTERNAL browser (`window.open(href,'_system')` → Capacitor → Safari/Chrome) instead of the in-app drawer; buyer pays out-of-app via BDO/GCash at the BASE price. Web byte-identical (isNativeApp false outside the WebView). **NET: app & web both = base price** (no markup, no Apple/Google cut, 0% processor via manual BDO/GCash reconciliation); the app is a doorway to web payment. The +30% markup (`lib/platform-pricing.ts`, #1458) is RETIRED. tsc green; native-only (no browser-preview path). **Follow-up flagged:** auth continuity on the external-browser hand-off (separate cookie jar → may need re-login; a one-time deep-link/magic-link smooths it) — do before iOS ships. NO auto-merge (App-Store-policy-sensitive). In `HeroVideoScrub.tsx` the frame is no longer a pure function of scroll position — a delta-time, SPEED-CAPPED rAF loop chases the scroll target: (1) **`MIN_PLAY_SECONDS`=5 + `MAX_RATE`=1/5** caps advance at ≤1/5 progress-per-second → a full play-through ALWAYS takes ≥5s no matter how fast you swipe (keeps gliding at the capped rate after the finger stops; a slow scrub stays under the cap → still tracks scroll 1:1; `EASE_PER_SEC`=6 softens the settle). Robust because `PostHeroReveal` collapses below-hero content to 0 height → a fling LANDS at the hero end + stays pinned, so it finishes on-screen, not scrolled away. (2) **`TRACK_VH` 300→700** = runway for a deliberate slow scrub. Checklist never asks "set your date" as step 1 — it guides: shortlist venues → find the date both share → lock it. The `/find-date` Schedule Matrix is the central mechanism. **(2) Reception venue is the Tier 1 anchor.** It constrains capacity, date window, and budget ceiling more than any other vendor. Shortlisted and deposited BEFORE ceremony venue in both Phase 1 (shortlisting at 480d) and Phase 2 (deposit at 330d). **(3) Three-tier budget model** — Tier 1: `reception_venue` (anchor); Tier 2: the 4 Big (`ceremony_venue`, `catering`, `coordinator`, `photo_video`, ~60–75% of the total budget); Tier 3: the rest of the event-type taxonomy (NOT a hardcoded list — computed from the couple's `interested_categories` picks filtered through the active event type's plan-group tree, minus Tier 1+2; different event types → different Tier 3). **(4) Paperwork is a separate budget line** — `marriage_license`, `psa_cenomar`, `church_fee` (Catholic only), `pre_cana` (Catholic only). Estimated from `ceremony_type` + `region`. **(5) Onboarding pre-fills the checklist.** `estimated_pax` → `guest_estimate` auto-completes; `estimated_budget_centavos` → `set_budget` auto-completes; `interested_categories` seeds the Tier 3 budget scope. Budget task copy reflects this: "Review your budget — Setnayan estimated one from your recommended services." **(6) Adaptive state machine per vendor category:** `not_started → needs_decision → searching → needs_more_options / one_option / in_progress → done` (or `excluded` / `deferred`). Decision prompt: "[Let's look for one] · [Definite No] · [Not sure yet]". Persisted in new `event_category_decisions` table (build queued). **(7) Budget health-check:** `buffer = estimated_budget − (tier1 + tier2 + tier3 + paperwork)`. Buffer ≥ 0 = good; buffer < 0 = show 3 options (increase budget / find cheaper / remove category). **(8) No-results state** — 4 options: Negotiate / Increase budget / Find cheaper / Add from outside + invite to Setnayan. **(9) Negotiation path** — pre-drafted message, sent via the in-app vendor-customer chat thread. One active negotiation per vendor at a time (anti-bombarding rule). All planning actions (negotiation start, budget decisions, lock events) logged in the chat thread as the audit trail. **(10) Budget + guest count moved to Phase 1** (495d/490d, before venue shortlisting at 480d/470d) — you can't evaluate a venue without knowing your headcount or budget. | 2026-06-20 | **Tax-aware pricing floor — STANDING pricing-governance rule (owner: "we should always have the tax-aware pricing floor").** Every priced SKU must clear `price ≥ (cost + target_margin) ÷ (1 − 0.30 − 0.037)`. The stack: **30% income-tax reserve** (conservative planning convention; accountant picks 8%-flat vs graduated) **+ ~3% BIR percentage tax + ~0.5–0.75% LGU business permit/LBT** (both scale with GROSS, the permit renews annually on prior-year sales) ≈ **~3.7% gross levies off the top, then 30% on the rest.** Core principle: **MARGIN = tax-survivability** — high-margin digital SKUs (Papic/monogram/AI/websites ~95–99%) shrug off the stack; low-margin commodity lines (storage/hardware) die (the ~3.7% gross levy alone can exceed the margin; e.g. 1 TB storage @ ₱899 vs ₱855 R2 cost nets ~₱8/mo). Locked consequences: (1) build on high-margin digital SKUs, never a thin-margin commodity line; (2) **storage = baked into the Pro tier, NOT sold** — any upgrade priced near-cost as retention (you can't out-price iCloud's ₱599/2TB = ₱0.29/GB, which is below our ₱0.855/GB wholesale). Supersedes the earlier ₱499–2,499 storage-upgrade ladder sketch. | `Pricing_Collection_2026-06-14.md` §11.A · [[project_setnayan_pricing_admin_managed]] · [[feedback_setnayan_pricing_holistic_review_later]] · [[project_setnayan_marginal_cost_model]] |

| 2026-06-20 | **Repo doc-contract change: per-PR CHANGELOG fragments kill the merge treadmill (owner sign-off requested).** Every feature PR prepended to the top of `CHANGELOG.md` + `STATUS.md`, so any two concurrent PRs conflicted by construction. `.gitattributes` already had `CHANGELOG.md merge=union`, but that only resolves LOCAL merges — **GitHub's auto-merge ignores `.gitattributes` merge drivers**, so in-flight PRs kept flipping to `CONFLICTING` and stalled until hand-merged. Verified the real lever: branch protection is **non-strict** (`required_status_checks.strict=false`), so a merely-*behind* PR auto-merges once green — the ONLY blocker is the `CONFLICTING` state. Fix = news-fragment pattern: each PR writes a unique `changelog.d/<slug>.md` file (can't collide) → PRs go `BEHIND` not `CONFLICTING` → auto-merge fires unattended. Added `changelog.d/` + README + `scripts/changelog-collect.mjs` (folds fragments → CHANGELOG.md at release, no deps), updated repo `CLAUDE.md` doc-contract (feature PRs add a fragment, do NOT edit CHANGELOG.md/STATUS.md directly; STATUS.md = refreshed snapshot, not a per-PR log), kept the union driver as belt-and-suspenders. ⚠ CHANGES HOW EVERY FUTURE SESSION RECORDS CHANGES — surfaced for owner sign-off. The 3 in-flight UX PRs (#1880/#1882/#1885) predate this and still use the old style; the fix applies going forward. | PR `claude/changelog-merge-fix` · `changelog.d/` · `scripts/changelog-collect.mjs` · repo `CLAUDE.md` · `.gitattributes` · [[project_setnayan_merge_workflow_reality]] |

| 2026-06-21 | **Vector Monogram Studio: fixed the PRODUCTION "not loading" race + reduced the page to studio-only (owner "vector studio is not working… make the vector monogram the only screen for the monogram. and make it work" — reported STILL broken on live prod).** Root cause is **production-valid, NOT dev-only StrictMode** (root-caused via a 7-agent parallel workflow + a real `next build`/`next start` repro): the imperative paper.js/opentype.js engine's editor DOM was injected via React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: STUDIO_HTML}}`. React's reconciler re-applies that prop whenever its **object reference** changes, and an inline `{{__html}}` literal is a NEW object every render — so the effect's own `setReady(true)` re-render re-set the host's `innerHTML`, re-creating the `#cv`/`#load`/`#names` nodes. The engine's **async font-fetch boot** (mountStudio returns sync; boots in `loadFont('cardo').then`) then fired against the now-DETACHED nodes → hid a detached overlay + drew on a detached canvas (visible overlay stuck on "Loading the typeface…", canvas blank) while the name write landed on the surviving input (real name still showed — the exact reported paradox). The earlier StrictMode/300×150 explanation + 2026-06-19 15s `failTimer` were both incomplete band-aids. **Fix:** the effect now OWNS the editor DOM (`root.innerHTML = STUDIO_HTML` + empty JSX div, wiped on cleanup) in BOTH wrappers, so React never reconciles the subtree. **Engine hardened:** a `destroyed` flag set in `destroy()` bails all async `loadFont` callbacks, closing the unmount-mid-fetch (route-nav-away) race the wrapper fix alone leaves open; + an idempotency guard. **Verified in a real production build** (`/monogram`: overlay hidden, full-res 1032×1360 canvas, monogram painted, interactions repaint). **Product change:** Vector Studio is now the ONLY content of `/dashboard/[eventId]/monogram` — removed the "Upload your own" card, the Feature-Us opt-in, AND the paid "How it animates" upsell (Animated Monogram stays in the Studio add-ons hub); deleted orphaned `upload-card.tsx`. | 2026-06-22 | **STD veil double-audio fixed — iOS-only "video + background music at the same time" on the Save-the-Date (owner-reported on /cale-ice).** The content film keeps the couple's keepsake clip WARM before its beat (unmuted at `volume=0`, looping, invisible) so its audio can crossfade in on the beat. That silencing assumes `volume=0` silences the clip — true on desktop/Android, but **iOS Safari treats `HTMLMediaElement.volume` as read-only** (system volume only): the write is ignored, the getter returns 1, so the warm invisible clip played at FULL volume under the soundtrack the moment the veil lifted. Music-side ducking was fine (it silences by `pause()`, honored on iOS); only the warm clip's volume-0 silence was broken. Regression from the warm-play feature (commit `52ec8ef5`, 2026-06-21) — hence "wasn't an issue before." **Fix (iOS-gated; desktop/Android byte-for-byte unchanged):** new `silenceWarmClip()` helper sets `volume=0`, reads it back, and falls back to `muted=true` where the write didn't stick (iOS); records controllability in `videoVolCtlRef`. Both warm-play sites route through it (warm clip never audible while hidden). The video beat reads the ref: controllable → existing smooth crossfade; not controllable (iOS) → play the clip MUTED, keep the soundtrack as the beat's audio (no dead air), surface the existing "Tap for sound" one-tap fallback. Net: no platform plays clip audio + soundtrack simultaneously. tsc 0 · lint clean · esbuild ok. | 2026-06-23 | **Papic / Alaala memory-economics — OWNER-LOCKED (design decision; ₱ figures ILLUSTRATIVE/PROVISIONAL → holistic pass; build is NET-NEW, not as-built).** Resolved across a long owner working session that stress-tested free Papic from ~8 angles (earn-nothing · exploit · multi-account farm · couple-gets-it-free-via-Drive · pay-everyone's-storage · perpetual-cost-accumulation). **① "Pay to create, free to keep, NO ADS":** Papic CAPTURE/creation (event capture + tagging-at-scale + reveal + SDE) is PAID (high-value, real cost to deliver); the finished CURATED MEMORY — one "post" per event = highlight reel + best ~100–200 photos + story (~1 GB, ~₱25/yr illustrative) — is KEPT FREE FOR LIFE (the emotional moat); **NO ads** (yield ~₱5–20K/mo even at scale + wrecks the private/premium keepsake brand; display ads already retired). Rationale: a one-time event payment (~₱3,000 illus.) CANNOT fund perpetual, accumulating raw storage (~3,000 items ≈ ~30 GB ≈ ~₱300/yr/event → consumes the payment in ~9 yrs then bleeds, compounding per event) — so charge for CREATION, keep only the cheap curated MEMORY. Setnayan = TikTok/Insta-like (each post a memory) but **EVENT-DRIVEN** (one post per event) + **PRIVATE-by-default** → orders-of-magnitude less storage/user → free-for-life is sustainable WITHOUT ads. **② Editorial self-contained in R2; raw firehose Drive-or-Vault:** the curated editorial NEVER links into the couple's Google Drive (moving/deleting Drive files must not break it) — anything curated INTO the editorial is COPIED into R2 (promote raw→editorial). RAW extras live Drive-only (₱0 to Setnayan) OR, if the couple wants Setnayan to host the full raw archive, an OPTIONAL paid annual **Alaala Vault** subscription (recurring cost = recurring fee). REFINES the 2026-06-03 "everything on R2 · Drive = copy" lock → now **R2 = system of record for the CURATED MEMORY (small, durable, free-for-life); RAW firehose = Drive-only (free) or Vault (paid)**, moving the expensive bulk OFF Setnayan's perpetual books. **The free editorial content budget IS the free-storage "limit".** ⚠ NOT AS-BUILT: the shipped free sampler (3 seats / 8 photos + 2 clips / 30-day, [[project_setnayan_papic_free_sampler]]) does NOT implement this split + has a verified storage-leak bug; the curated/raw split + editorial-promote-copy mechanic + Vault are NET-NEW build targets. ⚠ STAGING: Alaala Vault is revamp-derived ([[project_setnayan_alaala_revamp_strategy]] 2026-06-23 staging rule) — this row RECORDS the owner lock; corpus/live-canon integration + build wait for the post-session revamp pass. | DECISION_LOG (this row) · memory [[project_setnayan_storage_drive_copy_architecture]] (2026-06-23 addendum) + [[project_setnayan_papic_free_sampler]] · owner working session 2026-06-23 · ties [[project_setnayan_marginal_cost_model]] [[project_setnayan_pricing_tiers]] |

(2) **No build-skip** → **enabled built-in "Skip deployments when no changes to root dir or its dependencies"** (Turborepo-graph-aware; `turbo-ignore` is deprecated; Ignored Build Step left on Automatic). Amplifier = the parallel multi-agent PR firehose (PRs #2624→#2635 in ~4 hrs, many `claude/*` preview branches, every push rebuilds). **Guardrails going forward:** keep Build Machine Elastic/Standard (never Enhanced/Turbo — Turbo is Turbopack-only, we're on webpack); keep Skip-deployments ON; batch agent pushes; leave Observability Plus ON ($0.35, and disabling it blocks deploys). | 2026-07-03 | **QR-in-media integrity guard (owner-locked): the QR generators are the ONLY free customer-import channel for vendors — and vendors may NOT embed their QR codes in the photos/videos they upload to their website.** Rule as stated: "we will collect all their active QR codes and will check all the photos they upload on their website; if the QR code is there, the photo/video is invalid." Rationale: a vendor who prints their Shortlist/invite QR into portfolio media on `/v/[slug]` turns the marketplace page into a self-serve import funnel — marketplace visitors scan and enter as `source='vendor_invite'` "imports," dodging the inquiry path (burn-to-answer economics) and cheapening the "Verified booking" badge; the QR channel is FOR already-closed off-platform clients, in person. **What "all their active QR codes" means in shipped code:** (1) Shortlist/invite QR = deterministic `buildVendorInviteUrl` → any URL under `/vendor-invite/<their-slug>` (all `et`/`cat` variants — prefix-match, no storage needed); (2) Locked QR = the vendor's active single-use tokens minted by `issueLockedQr` (`lib/vendor-locked-qr` registry). Deliberately scoped to the VENDOR'S OWN codes — real wedding portfolio photos legitimately contain guest/table/event QR codes (Papic is QR-heavy); those must NOT invalidate media. **Enforcement shape (proposed, not yet built):** decode QR from every image upload on vendor-website surfaces (hero, portfolio, service-card showcase photos + the ≤30s clip via frame sampling ~1–2 fps) using a WASM QR decoder; client-side via the #2657 `validateFile` hook for instant feedback + a SERVER-side backstop (client is bypassable); match decoded payload → `/vendor-invite/<slug>` prefix OR active locked-QR token → reject with a clear message; plus a one-time retro-scan of already-uploaded media → admin review queue, not silent deletion. ⚠ Open sign-offs: (a) redirect loophole — exact self-QR matching misses a shortener QR (bit.ly → their invite URL); stricter option = reject ANY decodable QR that resolves to a setnayan.com vendor-invite/claim URL, or ANY QR at all on vendor-website media (recommend at least resolving same-host URLs); (b) "invalid" semantics = reject-at-upload (recommended) vs quarantine-for-admin; (c) whether the guard also covers editorial/moodboard media vendors can surface publicly. | 2026-07-16 | **Creator AUDIENCE layer SHIPPED — viewer counts + lightweight follow + notify-on-new-chapter.** Owner 2026-07-16: "creator = user; the differentiator is followers/viewers." Builds on the user-native refactor (PR #3314). **Viewer counts (aggregate, privacy-safe — no PII, no per-viewer row):** `creator_chapters.view_count` + `users.profile_view_count` BIGINT counters, bumped by two atomic self-gated SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (`increment_chapter_view`/`increment_profile_view`) that NO-OP on a draft chapter or hidden profile (a counter can never be inflated for a non-public target); granted `service_role` only (mirrors `increment_discount_uses`). Counted from a client `ViewBeacon` island → `recordChapterView`/`recordProfileView` server actions via the service-role admin client, keeping the ISR-cacheable `/u` + chapter pages off the cookie/auth hot path — CRON-FREE (a plain per-view UPDATE, no scheduler). Light dedup via a first-party httpOnly rolling cookie (cap 60 ids) avoids refresh-spam. Counts render on the chapter detail, timeline cards, and profile header. **Lightweight follow:** `user_follows(follower_user_id, followed_user_id, UNIQUE, CHECK follower<>followed)` — RLS Pattern A (follower owns their rows: `follower_user_id = auth.uid()` for select/insert/delete) + admin override; the follow GRAPH is PRIVATE (a caller reads only their own follows; who-follows-whom is never publicly queryable). `users.followers_count` — the ONLY publicly-surfaced audience number — is maintained by an AFTER INSERT/DELETE trigger (`sync_user_followers_count`, SECURITY DEFINER, clamped ≥0), so `/u` reads the aggregate WITHOUT touching the graph. Follow/Unfollow = `getFollowState`/`followUser`/`unfollowUser` server actions + a `FollowButton` client island shown ONLY to a signed-in visitor viewing SOMEONE ELSE'S public profile (never self/signed-out); follow guarded to public-profile targets; idempotent (unique-violation → no-op). **Notify-on-new-chapter (REUSES 0028 pipeline):** new `new_chapter_from_followed` notification type (separate enum migration so the value commits before runtime use); on publish (draft→published ONLY), `lib/creator-notify` fans out via `emitNotification` to the author's followers (follower lookup runs service-role — the author is the FOLLOWED party) from `after()` so it never blocks the publish. In-app for all followers; EMAIL consent-gated via a new `MARKETING_GATED_EMAIL_TYPES` set — an opted-out follower still gets the in-app notification but NO email (RA 10173, engagement ≠ transactional). Locked constraints honored: canonical RLS Pattern A + 4 helpers only; RLS at CREATE; no entity-ID change (`user_follows` is internal plumbing — hidden bigserial, no S89 public_id); cron-free (no new Vercel cron); no face/religion/minor field touched. | 2026-07-16 | **Creator Economy P1 SHIPPED — vendor↔creator DISCOUNT COLLAB loop (token-gated offer → accept → profile influence).** Owner 2026-07-16: "code it now around everybody." First rung of the three-party money engine in `Creator_Economy_Discount_Collab_Build_Plan_2026-07-16.md`, built on the user-native creator + audience layers (#3314/#3315). A vendor spends a REACH TOKEN to send a discount offer to a creator (any user with ≥1 published Adventure Chapter on a public profile); the creator accepts/declines; an accepted collab surfaces as aggregate "influence" on the creator's public profile. **Setnayan holds NO money** — it records the collab + gates outreach with a token; discounts settle off-platform (no payout/commission path). **#1 red line honored — REUSE, NOT FORK:** the reach-token spend reuses the EXISTING per-voucher burn (`consume_vendor_assets_per_voucher` founder / `consume_member_purchased_tokens` member) fronted by the SAME hold-and-release shape as fake-inquiry protection (`lead_token_holds`, 20270726988829). The `vendor_creator_offers` ROW is its own hold ledger (no new table/wallet/token primitive): send RESERVES a token (`offer_creator_reach_hold`, mirroring `unlock_vendor_event_hold`'s answering-member gate + soft reservation against the SAME wallet sources minus outstanding lead-holds AND offer-holds), accept/decline CONSUMES it (best-effort — a vendor overspend never blocks the creator), expiry past `expires_at` RELEASES it (refund) via cron-free `sweep_expired_creator_offers` wired into the vendor-dashboard `after()` (durable daily claim on `platform_settings.creator_offer_sweep_last_run_at`, mirrors `maybeSweepGhostedLeadHolds`). Schema migration `20270817214733_vendor_creator_offers_collab_p1.sql`: RLS at CREATE, canonical patterns only — SELECT = vendor via `current_vendor_ids('viewer')` OR addressed creator (`creator_user_id=auth.uid()`) OR `is_admin()`; admin-all override; NO public read; all mutations via SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (`offer_creator_reach_hold`/`respond_creator_offer`/`link_creator_offer_deliverable`/`sweep_expired_creator_offers`). Surfaces: **vendor** `/vendor-dashboard/creators` (doorway = My Shop tools card) browse eligible creators (reach ≥ vendor-set bar, ordered by followers/views) + send token-gated offer (creator rate + optional audience rate) + sent-offers status; **creator** offers inbox on `/dashboard/creator` (Accept/Decline; on accept may credit vendor in a published chapter = the deliverable, simple linkage); **profile** `/u/[userSlug]` aggregate "Partnered with" strip (name/logo → `/v/[slug]`, terms-free — never exposes offer terms or the graph). Two transactional notification types (`creator_offer_received`/`creator_offer_responded`) reuse the 0028 pipeline. **DEFERRED:** P2 viewer promo + attribution (audience-rate Book CTA → chapter-tagged lead unlocked with an existing lead token); P3 vendor ROI line (bookings driven/tokens spent) + bookings-driven influence. | 2026-07-25 | **🔒 LIVE STUDIO CHANNEL MODEL LOCKED — the broadcast goes on the COUPLE'S OWN YouTube channel; the "Setnayan-owned channel pool" is RETIRED as the default.** Owner considered and chose the Setnayan-owned pool first, then reversed on the operational reality: **a channel per event is not buildable.** Google rate-limits channel creation, each channel needs phone verification **plus a 24-hour wait before its first live stream**, and each is another OAuth token to hold — so a pool cannot scale past a handful. And "one channel per event" was the *only* thing that made the pool safe: concentrating N weddings on one channel means one reception's copyright strike takes **all N** down (3 strikes in 90 days = termination, and every VOD on it dies). **Couple's-own-channel is what was already SHIPPED** (`/api/oauth/youtube/start` 403s anyone whose `event_members.member_type ≠ 'couple'`), scales infinitely because every couple brings their own channel, and moves copyright exposure to whoever chose the music. It also sidesteps an **unresolved YouTube API Services ToS question**: enabling a user to stream to *their own* channel is unambiguously fine; hosting many paying customers' events on *your* channels via the API is a different shape, and the downside there is **API project suspension** (kills every event at once), not a survivable strike. ⚠ **`Live_Studio_Roam_RESUME_2026-07-23.md` still says "Roam streams on a Setnayan-owned YouTube channel pool" — that line is SUPERSEDED.** `live_studio_roam_channel_pool` exists (spine #3588) but holds **0 rows** and its admin registration screen was never built; leave it dormant. A small 5–10 channel pool may return later purely as a **fallback for couples who have no channel** — contained blast radius, built only when event volume justifies it. **ONBOARDING CONSEQUENCE (do not lose):** enabling live streaming on the couple's channel needs phone verification **+ a 24-hour wait**, so it must be surfaced as a do-it-now step at Live Studio purchase, never on the wedding morning. Content ID nuance recorded: claims (mute/monetize/region-block) are survivable and NOT strikes; live Content ID can **interrupt a stream mid-ceremony** if the rights-holder policy is "block" — same risk on either channel, so it is an operational-fallback problem, not a channel-choice one. | `apps/web/app/api/oauth/youtube/start/route.ts` · `Live_Studio_Roam_RESUME_2026-07-23.md` (superseded line) · `Live_Studio_Unified_Spec_2026-07-25.md` (left "YouTube channel/OAuth" as an open gate — this closes it) · PR #3703 / #3708 homepage + privacy copy already match this model |

So a cut on the unified controller reached the host's monitor and stopped: no window for OBS, no YouTube. Wave 5 installs the **same** bridge from the unified controller (no fork) and subscribes to **Wave 4's shared WebRTC viewer** (the transport is one-publisher→one-viewer per slot; a second viewer would steal the phones from the host's own monitor mid-ceremony). 🚨 **BUT THE PATH ITSELF OPENS A BYPASS, and closing it is the load-bearing half.** Wave 3's paywall stands on surfaces Setnayan OWNS (the `live_studio_roam_manifest` write + read gates). **The program output is a publication path we do NOT own** — the host's own OBS → the host's own YouTube. Under rehearse-free a host may legitimately cut between eight cameras; if those cuts reached the encoder, **rehearse-free would have meant BROADCAST-free via OBS** and the ₱2,999 product would be gone. **THE FIX — reduce the SOURCE, exactly as the manifest is reduced:** an un-entitled event's program frame carries **ONE camera, pinned to the host's ★ default and CUT-BLIND** (`decideProgramAir` / `programSourceAllowed`, in `lib/live-studio-publish.ts` beside `decidePublish`, which they REUSE for the count so there is one answer to "may this host broadcast multi-cam"). ⚠ **The pin deliberately IGNORES the cut** — unlike `limitPublishedManifest`, which uses the cut-aware `selectMainStageZone` because that path re-mirrors a manifest per provisioning cycle. Here the frame updates in real time, so honouring the cut would hand a free host **a live vision mixer**, which *is* the paid product. Rehearsal is NOT walked back: the controller monitor still follows every cut at full brightness (§ 4d). **Enforced server-side TWICE from the same helper** — the controller only publishes a permitted slot, and the pop-out independently re-resolves the decision on its own render and refuses to paint anything else (the bridge is a plain `window` property in the host's browser; trusting it would make the paywall a suggestion). Survives a direct PostgREST PATCH: `live_studio_roam_zones` UPDATE RLS **is** row-level and the anon key **is** public, so a host can rewrite `is_featured`/`is_main_stage`/`status` — and may, because those only choose WHICH channel the pin lands on; the COUNT comes from `orders`, which `orders_insert/update_status_guard` (`20270920010000`) makes unforgeable. **Free single-cam broadcasting untouched** (`panood_watch_url` not touched; one camera is never withheld) and **nothing cut → nothing on air**, free tier included. **Nothing faked:** a refused source shows a named "Unlock to broadcast all your cameras" card, never a black frame; a permitted-but-not-the-cut frame names the channel actually on air. Also fixed in passing: the program route now resolves entitlement with the **service-role** client (`orders` RLS is purchaser-scoped, so a coordinator running the encoder for a couple who PAID was reading "not owned" and would have been downgraded mid-wedding), and its host gate accepts the unified controller's wider predicate so a pop-out can never be stricter than the screen that opened it. **⚠ TWO LIMITS STATED, NOT HIDDEN:** (1) rehearse-free means every camera's media reaches the host's own browser **by design** — a host who rewrites their own browser's JavaScript can composite their own feeds; what is guaranteed is that **no shipped Setnayan code path** produces a multi-cam program frame for an un-entitled event. (2) A host could window-capture the CONTROLLER and crop to the CH 1 monitor, which follows every cut by owner lock (§ 4d "no dimming") — yielding a chrome-cropped, low-res and **SILENT** feed (controller monitors are `muted` by construction; the pop-out is the only surface carrying audio). Sealing makes the verdict cover exactly the bytes the guest receives; it does not make a poster-derived verdict a statement about the video's content. A host uploading a dirty video with a clean, unrelated poster still gets an approval — bound, sealed, and wrong. What the refix removes is *any clean JPEG from anywhere*: the poster must be this event's own `std-video-poster` object. | 2026-07-26 | **🔑 ROOT CAUSE NAMED — `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants `arwdDxtm` to `anon` AND `authenticated` on EVERY new relation in `public`. This is the engine behind "361 of 368 tables grant SELECT+INSERT to anon", and it bit the SEC-2b fix itself (PR #3747).** Migration `20271008731642` (SEC-2b, merged in #3736) **could not apply**: its own post-condition (g) `events_host-is-writable` rejected it, blocking main's entire migration pipeline behind it. Cause: `select defaclacl from pg_default_acl d join pg_namespace n on n.oid=d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname='public'` returns `anon=arwdDxtm/postgres | authenticated=arwdDxtm/postgres` — INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER — for every newly created relation. **A view is a relation**, so `CREATE VIEW public.events_host` handed `authenticated` the full set BEFORE the grant block ran, and `GRANT SELECT` **adds** a privilege rather than reducing the others. The migration revoked from `PUBLIC` and from `anon` **but not from `authenticated`**, leaving it holding UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE on an **auto-updatable, `security_invoker = false`** view — a write path straight past `couple_can_update_event` **and past RLS on `public.events`**. Eighth finding of the 2026-07-26 audit; eighth instance of the same single mistake — RLS is ROW-level and can NEVER hide a COLUMN (PR #3741).** `public.oauth_grants` stores Google credentials in **plaintext** (`refresh_token`, `access_token`). Verified against the live catalog: table-level `SELECT` granted to **both** `anon` and `authenticated`, and `has_column_privilege(…,'SELECT')` returning **true for every column of the table** for both roles — tokens included. RLS was on, with two PERMISSIVE policies both `TO authenticated` (`admin_manages_oauth_grants` = `is_admin()` cmd `*`; `event_member_reads_oauth_grants` = `event_id IN current_couple_event_ids()`, SELECT). **`anon` was never the exposure** — no policy names it, so it matches zero rows. **`authenticated` was:** the couple-read policy admits every couple member of the event to the ROW, and nothing then withheld the COLUMN, so `GET /rest/v1/oauth_grants?select=refresh_token` returned a live, long-lived Google credential — with curl, without ever loading a Setnayan page. **SCALE, STATED HONESTLY:** one signup ever and no evidence of any breach, so today the only person who can do this is reading their own token; the reason to fix it now is what it becomes at 5,000 weddings — **partner A can lift partner B's Drive refresh token**, a bearer credential to the connected Google account that outlives the wedding and cannot be un-leaked. **THE FIX is a column revoke, not a policy change:** the row policy is *correct* — tightening it would break the couple-facing "Connected to Drive as …" surfaces, which legitimately read `external_account_display`/`granted_at`/`connection_health`/`metadata` off the same rows. Only two columns are wrong. `metadata` was inspected against the live rows (`picture_url`, `account_name`, `drive_folder_id`, `drive_subfolders`, `drive_folder_name`, `thumbnail_url`) — **no token material**, so it stays readable. **NOTHING HAD TO MOVE:** all seven token readers were audited and every one already uses `createAdminClient()` (`/api/cron/oauth-refresh`, the drive/youtube/photo-delivery disconnect routes, the `disconnectPhotoDelivery` server action, `lib/drive-copy.ts`, `lib/photo-delivery-release.ts`); the three OAuth callbacks write tokens, also on the admin client — so connect, refresh and disconnect are unaffected, asserted by a `service_role` differential control rather than assumed. **WRITES DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE:** RLS gates writes ROW-wise and the only write policy is `is_admin()`, so a non-admin matches zero rows; the SELECT hole existed precisely *because* the read policy DOES match. ⚠ **STANDING RULE THIS GENERALISES (and the reason the same PR's two new columns shipped OPEN):** this project carries `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon, authenticated`, so **every new table, view, function AND COLUMN is reachable by the browser by default** — the freeze caught `event_paperwork.subject_user_id` + `oauth_grants.granted_by_user_id` at `anon=SIU authenticated=SIU`. Both are erasure-CONTROL inputs, not user data, and were revoked `SELECT`+`INSERT`+`UPDATE` **in the same migration that creates them** so column and lockdown cannot be cherry-picked apart. **`UPDATE` is the load-bearing one and it is the SEC-6 shape (a host-writable field feeding a server decision):** `event_paperwork`'s host policies are `TO PUBLIC` with `cmd=UPDATE`, so a writable `subject_user_id` would let a host stamp the **co-partner's** user id onto their own rows and have erasure destroy the co-partner's PSA/CENOMAR scan on the attacker's say-so — the exact harm the column was added to prevent, handed back through the front door. ⚠⚠ **AND THE TRAP INSIDE THE TRAP — the naive column `REVOKE` is a SILENT NO-OP.** Postgres: *"if a role has been granted privileges on a table, then revoking the same privileges from individual columns will have no effect."* With table-level `SELECT` held (prod's actual state) `REVOKE SELECT (refresh_token, access_token) … FROM anon, authenticated` applies cleanly and changes **nothing**. The shape is always **table-REVOKE-then-column-GRANT**, with the allow-list computed from **live** privileges so it unions with every earlier revoke instead of silently undoing one (the SEC-2b pattern from `20271008731642`). Both migrations carry post-conditions that `RAISE` on the no-op. 🧭 **THE MOST USEFUL LINE IN THE NEUTRALISATION TABLE IS THE ONE THAT PASSED:** probe **N2** (swap in the naive one-liner) scored **9/9 PASS — not caught**, because `20271009200000` runs first in the same PR and has already converted the table to a column-list grant, leaving the harness no table-level grant to fail against. **CI would have been green over a fix inert in production.** N2b (naive revoke *and* the earlier lockdown removed = prod's real state) makes the post-condition `RAISE` and all 9 fail. Prototype fixed: mobile track → `minmax(0,1fr)`, `.tiles` → `minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr)`, `min-width:0` on the layout children, long peso values `overflow-wrap:anywhere`. The guard is deliberately NOT applied to the two plain sorts, which is the whole reason `Lowest price` + `Top rated` stay **plain sorts, visually separated**: "Top rated" is an honest comparator the couple asked for, while the same words inside a recommendation would be Setnayan vouching for a vendor — and "Lowest price" could not be a weight vector anyway. **Below `MIN_DEMAND_COUPLE_COUNT` = 3 the "In demand" chip is REMOVED, not greyed** — every honest disabled wording either implies scarcity nothing measures or discloses the absence of other couples' activity on this couple's date. **Explainability is weight-aware** (§15.6): top dimension = `weight × (sub − NEUTRAL)`, the lift above neutral — under a raw `weight × sub` an all-unknown vendor always "wins" on refinement and every card falsely claims "Matches your style"; The derived "Also coming" strip's **Start planning** button hands the anchor straight in, so the pre-fill is the *anchor*, and the *celebration date* is always chosen. | 2026-08-10 | **FIXED — the 3-month floor now counts from the event's END.** Implements the ruling logged above. Date term is now `GREATEST(COALESCE(e.event_end_date, e.event_date), e.event_date) AS event_last_day`. **COALESCE** is the owner's fallback; **GREATEST is a one-way valve, not decoration** — `events_end_date_after_start` is a CHECK, and a CHECK can be dropped/NOT VALID/backfilled around, so a bare COALESCE would let a malformed end date EARLIER than the start expire those originals early. Wrapped, a bad end date can only be ignored. Postgres `GREATEST` ignores NULLs, so an event carrying only an end date floors on it instead of collapsing to "no floor"; the NULL escape hatch moved to the same derived term so the two cannot disagree. **The whole floor was swept, not just the SQL:** `lib/daily-email-jobs.ts` needed **no behavioural change and that is the point** — it calls the same rpc with both offsets pulled back, so the warning email followed with zero edits; a hand-typed copy there would have warned couples about a compression date the sweep no longer used, and warning LATER than the sweep runs is the direction that costs someone their originals. Latent in prod: 0 events carry a differing end date, so nothing changes for anyone today. | PR 9 · `20271126998711_retention_floor_counts_from_event_end.sql` · `apps/web/tests/db/papic-fullres-clock-event-end.db.test.ts` |
